description: By replacing thousands of equations with just one, ecology modelers can more accurately assess how close fragile environments are to a disastrous “tipping point.”

title: In Neural Networks, Unbreakable Locks Can Hide Invisible Doors
description: Cryptographers have shown how perfect security can undermine machine learning models.

title: An Applied Mathematician With an Unexpected Toolbox
description: Lek-Heng Lim uses tools from algebra, geometry and topology to answer questions in machine learning.

title: With Nothing to Eat Except Viruses, Some Microbes Thrive
description: “Virovores” — organisms that survive and multiply by eating viruses — might influence the flow of energy through ecosystems.

title: Quantum Field Theory Pries Open Mathematical Puzzle
description: Mathematicians have struggled to understand the moduli space of graphs. A new paper uses tools from physics to peek inside.

title: To Teach Computers Math, Researchers Merge AI Approaches
description: Large language models still struggle with basic reasoning tasks. Two new papers that apply machine learning to math provide a blueprint for how that could change.

title: Gene Expression in Neurons Solves a Brain Evolution Puzzle
description: The neocortex of our brain is the seat of our intellect. New data suggests that mammals created it with new types of cells that they developed only after their evolutionary split from reptiles.

title: She Studies Growing Arteries to Aid Heart Attack Recovery
description: Regenerative medicine researcher Kristy Red Horse’s discoveries may someday help damaged hearts heal better. Her stewardship of her Native American heritage may advance science in other ways too.

title: Researchers Discover a More Flexible Approach to Machine Learning
description: “Liquid” neural nets, based on a worm’s nervous system, can transform their underlying algorithms on the fly, giving them unprecedented speed and adaptability.

title: How Our Reality May Be a Sum of All Possible Realities
description: Richard Feynman’s path integral is both a powerful prediction machine and a philosophy about how the world is. But physicists are still struggling to figure out how to use it, and what it means.

title: Machines Learn Better if We Teach Them the Basics
description: A wave of research improves reinforcement learning algorithms by pre-training them as if they were human.

title: When Does the Brain Operate at Peak Performance?
description: The critical brain hypothesis suggests that neural networks do their best work when connections are not too weak or too strong.

title: Astronomers Say They Have Spotted the Universe’s First Stars
description: Theory has it that “Population III” stars brought light to the cosmos. The James Webb Space Telescope may have just glimpsed them.

title: How Quantum Physicists ‘Flipped Time’ (and How They Didn’t)
description: Two teams have made photons act as if time were simultaneously flowing in two directions. The experiments demonstrate a way to potentially boost the performance of quantum devices.

title: The Cause of Depression Is Probably Not What You Think
description: Depression has often been blamed on low levels of serotonin in the brain. That answer is insufficient, but alternatives are coming into view and changing our understanding of the disease.

title: Standard Model of Cosmology Survives a Telescope’s Surprising Finds
description: Reports that the James Webb Space Telescope killed the reigning cosmological model turn out to have been exaggerated. But astronomers still have much to learn from distant galaxies glimpsed by Webb.

title: Mathematicians Roll Dice and Get Rock-Paper-Scissors
description: Mathematicians have uncovered a surprising wealth of rock-paper-scissors-like patterns in randomly chosen dice.

title: Finally, a Fast Algorithm for Shortest Paths on Negative Graphs
description: Researchers can now find the shortest route through a network nearly as fast as theoretically possible, even when some steps can cancel out others.

title: Mobile Genes From the Mother Shape the Baby’s Microbiome
description: Tiny genetic sequences in a mother’s bacteria seem to hop into the infant's bacteria, perhaps ensuring a healthy microbiome later in life.

title: Probability and Number Theory Collide — in a Moment
description: Mathematicians are taking ideas developed to study random numbers and applying them to a broad range of categories.

title: Ants Live 10 Times Longer by Altering Their Insulin Responses
description: Queen ants live far longer than genetically identical workers. Researchers are learning what their longevity secrets could mean for aging in other species.

title: New Algorithm Closes Quantum Supremacy Window
description: Random circuit sampling, a popular technique for showing the power of quantum computers, doesn’t scale up if errors go unchecked.

title: The Physics Principle That Inspired Modern AI Art
description: Diffusion models generate incredible images by learning to reverse the process that, among other things, causes ink to spread through water.

title: The Year in Comments
description: While the internet is awash in the noise of unmoderated comments, Quanta has attempted to provide a quiet, information-rich spot where readers, listeners and viewers can contemplate the complexity of nature.

title: The Year in Math
description: Four Fields Medals were awarded for major breakthroughs in geometry, combinatorics, statistical physics and number theory, even as mathematicians continued to wrestle with how computers are changing the discipline.

title: ‘Fullertubes’ Join the Family of Carbon Crystals
description: The buckminsterfullerene revolution never came, but some researchers are eagerly exploring the properties of newfound carbon crystals known as fullertubes.

title: She Finds Keys to Ecology in Cells That Steal From Others
description: The ecologist Holly Moeller studies microorganisms that expand their range by absorbing organelles and gaining new metabolic talents from their prey.

title: ‘Nasty’ Geometry Breaks Decades-Old Tiling Conjecture
description: Mathematicians predicted that if they imposed enough restrictions on how a shape might tile space, they could force a periodic pattern to emerge. But they were wrong.

title: She Turns Fluids Into ‘Black Holes’ and ‘Inflating Universes’
description: By using fluids to model inaccessible realms of the cosmos, Silke Weinfurtner is “looking for a deeper truth beyond one system.” But what can such experiments teach us?

title: What Causes Alzheimer’s? Scientists Are Rethinking the Answer. (Pt. 2)
description: If plaques of amyloid protein in the brain aren’t the root cause of Alzheimer’s disease, what is?

title: What Causes Alzheimer’s? Scientists Are Rethinking the Answer.
description: After decades in the shadow of the reigning model for Alzheimer’s disease, alternative explanations are finally getting the attention they deserve.

title: Physicists Create a Holographic Wormhole Using a Quantum Computer
description: The unprecedented experiment explores the possibility that space-time somehow emerges from quantum information.

title: AI Reveals New Possibilities in Matrix Multiplication
description: Inspired by the results of a game-playing neural network, mathematicians have been making unexpected advances on an age-old math problem.

title: Why This Universe? A New Calculation Suggests Our Cosmos Is Typical.
description: Two physicists have calculated that the universe has a higher entropy — and is therefore more likely — than alternative possible universes.

title: Computer Proof ‘Blows Up’ Centuries-Old Fluid Equations
description: For more than 250 years, mathematicians have wondered if the Euler equations might sometimes fail to describe a fluid’s flow. A new computer-assisted proof marks a major breakthrough in that quest.

title: New Chip Expands the Possibilities for AI
description: An energy-efficient chip called NeuRRAM fixes an old design flaw to run large-scale AI algorithms on smaller devices, reaching the same accuracy as wasteful digital computers.

title: Cryptography’s Future Will Be Quantum-Safe. Here’s How It Will Work.
description: Lattice cryptography promises to protect secrets from the attacks of far-future quantum computers.

title: How Supergenes Fuel Evolution Despite Harmful Mutations
description: Supergenes that lock inherited traits together are widespread in nature. Recent work shows that their blend of genetic benefits and risks for species can be complex.

title: The Enduring Mystery of the Dragonfly 44 Galaxy
description: A growing catalog of huge but dim galaxies such as Dragonfly 44 is forcing astronomers to invent new theories of galactic evolution.

title: Ocean Bacteria Reveal an Unexpected Multicellular Form
description: Marine bacteria normally seen as single cells join together as a “microscopic snow globe” to consume bulky floating carbohydrates.

title: How Genes Can Leap From Snakes to Frogs in Madagascar
description: The discovery of a hot spot for horizontal gene transfer draws attention to the possible roles of parasites and ecology in such changes.

title: New Entanglement Results Hint at Better Quantum Codes
description: A team of physicists has entangled three photons over a considerable distance, which could lead to more powerful quantum cryptography.

title: Inside the Proton, the ‘Most Complicated Thing You Could Possibly Imagine’
description: The positively charged particle at the heart of the atom is an object of unspeakable complexity, one that changes its appearance depending on how it is probed.

title: The Computer Scientist Who’s Boosting Privacy on the Internet
description: Harry Halpin wants our internet conversations to be more private. He’s helped create a new kind of network that might make it possible.

title: Human Brains Are Hard to Study. He Grows Useful Substitutes.
description: With stem cell technology and lab-grown brain organoids, Sergiu Paşca seeks the causes of autism and other neuropsychiatric conditions.

title: Lab-Grown Human Cells Form Working Circuits in Rat Brains
description: Letting human brain organoids grow in animal brains could be an ethical new option for experimental studies of neurological disorders.

title: How Do You Prove a Secret?
description: Zero-knowledge proofs allow researchers to prove their knowledge without divulging the knowledge itself.

title: Machine Learning Highlights a Hidden Order in Scents
description: Efforts to build a better digital “nose” suggest that our perception of scents reflects both the structure of aromatic molecules and the metabolic processes that make them.

title: How Mathematical Curves Enable Advanced Communication
description: A simple geometric idea has been used to power advances in information theory, cryptography and even blockchain technology.

title: Chaos Researchers Can Now Predict Perilous Points of No Return
description: A custom-built machine learning algorithm can predict when a complex system is about to switch to a wildly different mode of behavior.

title: How Transformers Seem to Mimic Parts of the Brain
description: Neural networks originally designed for language processing turn out to be great models of how our brains understand places.

title: How Shannon Entropy Imposes Fundamental Limits on Communication
description: What’s a message, really? Claude Shannon recognized that the elemental ingredient is surprise.

title: How Isaac Newton Discovered the Binomial Power Series
description: Rethinking questions and chasing patterns led Newton to find the connection between curves and infinite sums.

title: The AI Researcher Giving Her Field Its Bitter Medicine
description: Anima Anandkumar wants computer scientists to move beyond the matrix, among other challenges.

title: Bacteria’s Immune Sensors Reveal a Novel Way to Detect Viruses
description: A new study reveals that bacteria can fight viruses in a surprisingly elegant way that has no known counterpart in more complex life.

title: ‘Post-Quantum’ Cryptography Scheme Is Cracked on a Laptop
description: Two researchers have broken an encryption protocol that many saw as a promising defense against the power of quantum computing.

title: What Drives Galaxies? The Milky Way’s Black Hole May Be the Key.
description: Supermassive black holes have come to the fore as engines of galactic evolution, but new observations of the Milky Way and its central hole don’t yet hang together.

title: Electric Fish Genomes Reveal How Evolution Repeats Itself
description: By studying how electric organs arose in different lineages of fish, scientists gain new insights into a long-standing question of evolutionary biology.

title: Epigenetic ‘Clocks’ Predict Animals’ True Biological Age
description: A statistical analysis of chemical tags on DNA may help unify disparate theories of aging.

title: Self-Taught AI Shows Similarities to How the Brain Works
description: Self-supervised learning allows a neural network to figure out for itself what matters. The process might be what makes our own brains so successful.

title: Particle Physicists Puzzle Over a New Duality
description: A hidden link has been found between two seemingly unrelated particle collision outcomes. It’s the latest example of a mysterious web of mathematical connections between disparate theories of physics.

title: Hidden Chaos Found to Lurk in Ecosystems
description: New research finds that chaos plays a bigger role in population dynamics than decades of ecological data seemed to suggest.

title: A Question About a Rotating Line Helps Reveal What Makes Real Numbers Special
description: The Kakeya conjecture predicts how much room you need to point a line in every direction. In one number system after another — with one important exception — mathematicians have been proving it true.

title: The Astrophysicist Who Sculpts Stars Before They Are Born
description: Nia Imara is working to understand the mysterious clouds of gas and dust that collapse into stars.

title: How the ‘Diamond of the Plant World’ Helped Land Plants Evolve
description: Structural studies of the robust material called sporopollenin reveal how it made plants hardy enough to reproduce on dry land.

title: Computer Science Proof Unveils Unexpected Form of Entanglement
description: Three computer scientists have posted a proof of the NLTS conjecture, showing that systems of entangled particles can remain difficult to analyze even away from extremes.

title: Hypergraphs Reveal Solution to 50-Year-Old Problem
description: In 1973, Paul Erdős asked if it was possible to assemble sets of “triples” — three points on a graph — so that they abide by two seemingly incompatible rules. A new proof shows it can always be done.

title: How Do Mathematicians Know Their Proofs Are Correct?
description: What makes a proof stronger than a guess? What does evidence look like in the realm of mathematical abstraction? Hear the mathematician Melanie Matchett Wood explain how probability helps to guide number theorists toward certainty.

title: Embryo Cells Set Patterns for Growth by Pushing and Pulling
description: Patterns that guide the development of feathers and other features can be set by mechanical forces in the embryo, not just by gradients of chemicals.

title: The Scientist Who Developed a New Way to Understand Communication
description: Mark Braverman has spent his career translating thorny problems into the language of information complexity.

title: For His Sporting Approach to Math, a Fields Medal
description: With Hugo Duminil-Copin, thinking rarely happens without moving. His insights into the flow-related properties of complex networks have earned him the Fields Medal.

title: He Dropped Out to Become a Poet. Now He’s Won a Fields Medal.
description: June Huh wasn’t interested in mathematics until a chance encounter during his sixth year of college. Now his profound insights connecting combinatorics and geometry have led to math’s highest honor.

title: In Times of Scarcity, War and Peace, a Ukrainian Finds the Magic in Math
description: With her homeland mired in war, the sphere-packing number theorist Maryna Viazovska has become the second woman to win a Fields Medal in the award’s 86-year history.

title: Can Computers Be Mathematicians?
description: Artificial intelligence has bested humans at problem-solving challenges like chess and Go. Is mathematics research next? Steven Strogatz speaks with mathematician Kevin Buzzard to learn about the effort to translate math into language that computers understand.

title: Protein Blobs Linked to Alzheimer’s Affect Aging in All Cells
description: Protein buildups like those seen around neurons in Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and other brain diseases occur in all aging cells, a new study suggests. Learning their significance may reveal new strategies for treating age-related diseases.

title: By Exploring Virtual Worlds, AI Learns in New Ways
description: Intelligent beings learn by interacting with the world. Artificial intelligence researchers have adopted a similar strategy to teach their virtual agents new tricks.

title: Mathematical Connect-the-Dots Reveals How Structure Emerges
description: A new proof identifies precisely how large a mathematical graph must be before it contains a regular substructure.

title: Wheel Made of ‘Odd Matter’ Spontaneously Rolls Uphill
description: Physicists have solved a key problem of robotic locomotion by revising the usual rules of interaction between simple component parts.

title: Researchers Achieve ‘Absurdly Fast’ Algorithm for Network Flow
description: Computer scientists can now solve a decades-old problem in practically the time it takes to write it down.

title: Reshuffled Rivers Bolster the Amazon’s Hyper-Biodiversity
description: The lush biodiversity of the Amazon may be due in part to the dynamics of branching rivers, which serve as invisible fences that continuously barricade and merge bird populations.

title: Brain-Signal Proteins Evolved Before Animals Did
description: Some animal neuropeptides have been around longer than nervous systems.

title: Surfaces Beyond Imagination Are Discovered After Decades-Long Search
description: Using ideas borrowed from graph theory, two mathematicians have shown that extremely complex surfaces are easy to traverse.

title: What Is the Langlands Program?
description: The Langlands program provides a beautifully intricate set of connections between various areas of mathematics, pointing the way toward novel solutions for old problems.

title: How to Make the Universe Think for Us
description: Physicists are building neural networks out of vibrations, voltages and lasers, arguing that the future of computing lies in exploiting the universe’s complex physical behaviors.

title: Physicists Rewrite the Fundamental Law That Leads to Disorder
description: The second law of thermodynamics is among the most sacred in all of science, but it has always rested on 19th century arguments about probability. New arguments trace its true source to the flows of quantum information.

title: How Computer Scientists Learned to Reinvent the Proof
description: Why verify every line of a proof, when just a few checks will do?

title: Simple Gene Circuits Hint at How Stem Cells Find New Identities
description: Synthetic biology experiments suggest a “MultiFate” model for how genetically identical cells become the many different types found in complex organisms like us.

title: How Complex Is a Knot? New Proof Reveals Ranking System That Works.
description: “Ribbon concordance” will let mathematicians compare knots by linking them across four-dimensional space.

title: How to Write Software With Mathematical Perfection
description: Leslie Lamport revolutionized how computers talk to each other. Now he’s working on how engineers talk to their machines.

title: Computer Scientists Prove That Certain Problems Are Truly Hard
description: Finding out whether a question is too difficult to ever solve efficiently depends on figuring out just how hard it is. Researchers have now shown how to do that for a major class of problems.

title: In Test Tubes, RNA Molecules Evolve Into a Tiny Ecosystem
description: When researchers gave a genetic molecule the ability to replicate, it evolved over time into a complex network of “hosts” and “parasites” that both competed and cooperated to survive.

title: Where Do Space, Time and Gravity Come From?
description: Einstein’s description of curved space-time doesn’t easily mesh with a universe made up of quantum wavefunctions. Theoretical physicist Sean Carroll discusses the quest for quantum gravity with host Steven Strogatz.

title: Mathematicians Coax Fluid Equations Into Nonphysical Solutions
description: The famed Navier-Stokes equations can lead to cases where more than one result is possible, but only in an extremely narrow set of situations.

title: What Happens When We Give Animals Our Diseases?
description: While it’s understandable to focus on the diseases affecting humans, it’s important to study how our illnesses may affect animals.

title: Ancient Genes for Symbiosis Hint at Mitochondria’s Origins
description: Was the addition of mitochondria a first step in the formation of complex cells or one of the last? A new study of bacteria tries to answer this contentious question in evolutionary biology.

title: Elegant Six-Page Proof Reveals the Emergence of Random Structure
description: Two young mathematicians have astonished their colleagues with a full proof of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture — a sweeping statement about how structure emerges in random sets and graphs.

title: In Sexy Worms, Inheritance Beyond Genes Can Help Evolution
description: Traits from RNA molecules passed between multiple generations of worms can work with genetic changes to influence future evolution.

title: Which Computational Universe Do We Live In?
description: Cryptographers want to know which of five possible worlds we inhabit, which will reveal whether truly secure cryptography is even possible.

title: Researchers Gain New Understanding From Simple AI
description: Language processing programs are notoriously hard to interpret, but smaller versions can provide important insights into how they work.

title: Scientists Unravel How the Tonga Volcano Caused Worldwide Tsunamis
description: The Tonga eruption in January was “basically like Krakatoa 2.” This time, geophysicists could explain the tiny tsunamis that cropped up all over the planet, solving a 139-year-old mystery about Tonga’s predecessor.

title: Deep Learning Poised to ‘Blow Up’ Famed Fluid Equations
description: For centuries, mathematicians have tried to prove that Euler’s fluid equations can produce nonsensical answers. A new approach to machine learning has researchers betting that “blowup” is near.

title: Newly Measured Particle Seems Heavy Enough to Break Known Physics
description: A new analysis of W bosons suggests these particles are significantly heavier than predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics.

title: Researchers Identify ‘Master Problem’ Underlying All Cryptography
description: The existence of secure cryptography depends on one of the oldest questions in computational complexity.

title: In Music and Math, Lillian Pierce Builds Landscapes
description: Lillian Pierce wants to transform access to the world of mathematics, while making headway on problems that bridge the discrete and continuous.

title: Massive Black Holes Shown to Act Like Quantum Particles
description: Physicists are using quantum math to understand what happens when black holes collide. In a surprise, they’ve shown that a single particle can describe a collision’s entire gravitational wave.

title: Cells Blaze Their Own Trails to Navigate Through the Body
description: With self-generated gradients of chemicals and physical tension, cells in the body steer themselves to vital destinations.

title: What a Math Party Game Tells Us About Graph Theory
description: Play this simple math game with your friends to gain insights into fundamental principles of graph theory.

title: A New Tool for Finding Dark Matter Digs Up Nothing
description: Physicists are devising clever new ways to exploit the extreme sensitivity of gravitational wave detectors like LIGO. But so far, they’ve seen no signs of exotica.

title: Machine Learning Reimagines the Building Blocks of Computing
description: Traditional algorithms power complicated computational tools like machine learning. A new approach, called algorithms with predictions, uses the power of machine learning to improve algorithms.

title: Will Transformers Take Over Artificial Intelligence?
description: A simple algorithm that revolutionizes how neural networks approach language is now taking on image classification as well. It may not stop there.

title: In New Math Proofs, Artificial Intelligence Plays to Win
description: A new computer program fashioned after artificial intelligence systems like AlphaGo has solved several open problems in combinatorics and graph theory.

title: Scientists Watch a Memory Form in a Living Brain
description: While watching a fearful memory take shape in the brain of a living fish, neuroscientists see an unexpected level of rewiring occur in the synaptic connections.

title: How We Can Make Sense of Chaos
description: Dynamical systems can be chaotic and impossible to predict, but mathematicians have discovered tools to help understand them.

title: Cryptographers Achieve Perfect Secrecy With Imperfect Devices
description: For the first time, experiments demonstrate the possibility of sharing secrets with perfect privacy — even when the devices used to share them cannot be trusted.

title: Most Complete Simulation of a Cell Probes Life’s Hidden Rules
description: A 3D digital model of a “minimal cell” leads scientists closer to understanding the barest requirements for life.

title: AI Overcomes Stumbling Block on Brain-Inspired Hardware
description: Algorithms that use the brain’s communication signal can now work on analog neuromorphic chips, which closely mimic our energy-efficient brains.

title: A Billion Years Before Sex, Ancient Cells Were Equipped for It
description: Molecular detective work is zeroing in on the origins of sexual reproduction. The protein tools for cell mergers seem to have long predated sex — so what were they doing?

title: Machine Learning Becomes a Mathematical Collaborator
description: Two recent collaborations between mathematicians and DeepMind demonstrate the potential of machine learning to help researchers generate new mathematical conjectures.

title: Computer Scientists Prove Why Bigger Neural Networks Do Better
description: Two researchers show that for neural networks to be able to remember better, they need far more parameters than previously thought.

title: Quantum Complexity Tamed by Machine Learning
description: If only scientists understood exactly how electrons act in molecules, they’d be able to predict the behavior of everything from experimental drugs to high-temperature superconductors. Following decades of physics-based insights, artificial intelligence systems are taking the next leap.

title: Machine Learning Gets a Quantum Speedup
description: Two teams have shown how quantum approaches can solve problems faster than classical computers, bringing physics and computer science closer together.

title: Secrets of Early Animal Evolution Revealed by Chromosome ‘Tectonics’
description: Large blocks of genes conserved through hundreds of millions of years of evolution hint at how the first animal chromosomes came to be.

title: A Solution to the Faint-Sun Paradox Reveals a Narrow Window for Life
description: We might have a past faint sun to owe for life’s existence. This has consequences for the possibility of life outside Earth.

title: Researchers Build AI That Builds AI
description: By using hypernetworks, researchers can now preemptively fine-tune artificial neural networks, saving some of the time and expense of training.

title: Any Single Galaxy Reveals the Composition of an Entire Universe
description: In computer simulations of possible universes, researchers have discovered that a neural network can infer the amount of matter in a whole universe by studying just one of its galaxies.

title: Computer Scientists Eliminate Pesky Quantum Computations
description: For years, intermediate measurements made it hard to quantify the complexity of quantum algorithms. New work establishes that those measurements aren’t necessary after all.

title: Symmetries Reveal Clues About the Holographic Universe
description: Physicists have been busy exploring how our universe might emerge like a hologram out of a two-dimensional sheet. New clues have come from the symmetries found on an infinitely distant “celestial sphere.”

title: Evolution ‘Landscapes’ Predict What’s Next for COVID Virus
description: Studies that map the adaptive value of viral mutations hint at how the COVID-19 pandemic might progress next.

title: Flying Fish and Aquarium Pets Yield Secrets of Evolution
description: New studies reveal the ancient, shared genetic “grammar” underpinning the diverse evolution of fish fins and tetrapod limbs.

title: An Injection of Chaos Solves Decades-Old Fluid Mystery
description: In the 1960s, drillers noticed that certain fluids would firm up if they flowed too fast. Researchers have finally explained why.

title: The Year in Biology
description: The detailed understanding of brains and multicellular bodies reached new heights this year, while the genomes of the COVID-19 virus and various organisms yielded more surprises.

title: Detailed Footage Finally Reveals What Triggers Lightning
description: Scientists have never been able to adequately explain where lightning comes from. Now the first detailed observations of its emergence inside a cloud have exposed how electric fields grow strong enough to let bolts fly.

title: Mathematician Hurls Structure and Disorder Into Century-Old Problem
description: A new paper shows how to create longer disordered strings than mathematicians had thought possible, proving that a well-known recent conjecture is “spectacularly wrong.”

title: When a Gene Illness Discovery Means Breaking Bad News
description: When scientists discover genes linked to dangerous illnesses in their samples, how should they convey that news to the study participants? The geneticist Cristen Willer had to tackle that challenge.

title: Mathematicians Transcend Geometric Theory of Motion
description: More than 30 years ago, Andreas Floer changed geometry. Now, two mathematicians have finally figured out how to extend his revolutionary perspective.

title: Gravitational Waves Should Permanently Distort Space-Time
description: The “gravitational memory effect” predicts that a passing gravitational wave should forever alter the structure of space-time. Physicists have linked the phenomenon to fundamental cosmic symmetries and a potential solution to the black hole information paradox.

title: AI Researchers Fight Noise by Turning to Biology
description: Tiny amounts of artificial noise can fool neural networks, but not humans. Some researchers are looking to neuroscience for a fix.

title: New Brain Maps Can Predict Behaviors
description: Rapid advances in large-scale connectomics are beginning to spotlight the importance of individual variations in the neural circuitry. They also highlight the limitations of “wiring diagrams” alone.

title: Researchers Defeat Randomness to Create Ideal Code
description: By carefully constructing a multidimensional and well-connected graph, a team of researchers has finally created a long-sought locally testable code that can immediately betray whether it’s been corrupted.

title: At the Dawn of Life, Heat May Have Driven Cell Division
description: A mathematical model shows how a thermodynamic mechanism could have made protocells split in two.

title: The Algorithm That Lets Particle Physicists Count Higher Than Two
description: Through his encyclopedic study of the electron, an obscure figure named Stefano Laporta found a handle on the subatomic world’s fearsome complexity. His algorithm has swept the field.

title: To Be Energy-Efficient, Brains Predict Their Perceptions
description: Results from neural networks support the idea that brains are “prediction machines” — and that they work that way to conserve energy.

title: A New Theory for Systems That Defy Newton’s Third Law
description: In nonreciprocal systems, where Newton’s third law falls apart, “exceptional points” are helping researchers understand phase transitions and possibly other phenomena.

title: Mathematicians Find Structure in Biased Polynomials
description: New work establishes a tighter connection between the rank of a polynomial and the extent to which it favors particular outputs.

title: Sponge Genes Hint at the Origins of Neurons and Other Cells
description: A new study of gene expression in sponges reveals the complex diversity of their cells as well as some possibly ancient connections between the nervous, immune and digestive systems.

title: Researchers Revise Recipe for Building a Rocky Planet Like Earth
description: Over the past decade, researchers have completely rewritten the story of how gas giants such as Jupiter and Saturn form. They’re now debating whether the same process might hold for Earth.

title: Her Machine Learning Tools Pull Insights From Cell Images
description: The computational biologist Anne Carpenter creates software that brings the power of machine learning to researchers seeking answers in mountains of cell images.

title: An Ultra-Precise Clock Links the Quantum World With Gravity
description: Time was found to flow differently between the top and bottom of a single cloud of atoms. Physicists hope that such a system will one day help them combine quantum mechanics and Einstein’s theory of gravity.

title: The Uselessness of Useful Knowledge
description: Today’s powerful but little-understood artificial intelligence breakthroughs echo past examples of unexpected scientific progress.

title: Neuron Bursts Can Mimic Famous AI Learning Strategy
description: A new model of learning centers on bursts of neural activity that act as teaching signals — approximating backpropagation, the algorithm behind learning in AI.

title: How Animals Map 3D Spaces Surprises Brain Researchers
description: When animals move through 3D spaces, the neat system of grid cell activity they use for navigating on flat surfaces gets more disorderly. That has implications for some ideas about memory and other processes.

title: How Wavelets Allow Researchers to Transform, and Understand, Data
description: Built upon the ubiquitous Fourier transform, the mathematical tools known as wavelets allow unprecedented analysis and understanding of continuous signals.

title: The Astronomer Who’s About to See the Skies of Other Earths
description: After the ultra-powerful James Webb Space Telescope launches later this year, Laura Kreidberg will lead two efforts to check the weather on rocky planets orbiting other stars.

title: A New Link to an Old Model Could Crack the Mystery of Deep Learning
description: To help them explain the shocking success of deep neural networks, researchers are turning to older but better-understood models of machine learning.

title: Mathematicians Prove Melting Ice Stays Smooth
description: After decades of effort, mathematicians now have a complete understanding of the complicated equations that model the motion of free boundaries, like the one between ice and water.

title: Work on Earth’s Climate and Other Complex Systems Earns Nobel Prize in Physics
description: Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann have been honored for their work that led to reliable predictions of the effects of climate change. They will share the Nobel with Giorgio Parisi, who has made pioneering studies of chaotic physical systems.

title: Anil Seth Finds Consciousness in Life’s Push Against Entropy
description: How does consciousness arise in mere flesh and blood? To the neuroscientist Anil Seth, our organic bodies are the key to the experience.

title: Single Cells Evolve Large Multicellular Forms in Just Two Years
description: Researchers have discovered that environments favoring clumpy growth are all that’s needed to quickly transform single-celled yeast into complex multicellular organisms.

title: Mathematical Analysis of Fruit Fly Wings Hints at Evolution’s Limits
description: A painstaking study of wing morphology shows both the striking uniformity of individuals in a species and a subtle pattern of linked variations that evolution can exploit.

title: Biologists Rethink the Logic Behind Cells’ Molecular Signals
description: The molecular signaling systems of complex cells are nothing like simple electronic circuits. The logic governing their operation is riotously complex — but it has advantages.

title: A Massive Subterranean ‘Tree’ Is Moving Magma to Earth’s Surface
description: Deep in the mantle, a branching plume of intensely hot material appears to be the engine powering vast volcanic activity.

title: How Computationally Complex Is a Single Neuron?
description: Computational neuroscientists taught an artificial neural network to imitate a biological neuron. The result offers a new way to think about the complexity of single brain cells.

title: The Complex Truth About ‘Junk DNA’
description: Genomes hold immense quantities of noncoding DNA. Some of it is essential for life, some seems useless, and some has its own agenda.

title: To Learn More Quickly, Brain Cells Break Their DNA
description: New work shows that neurons and other brain cells use DNA double-strand breaks, often associated with cancer, neurodegeneration and aging, to quickly express genes related to learning and memory.

title: How Big Data Carried Graph Theory Into New Dimensions
description: Researchers are turning to the mathematics of higher-order interactions to better model the complex connections within their data.

title: Computer Scientists Discover Limits of Major Research Algorithm
description: The most widely used technique for finding the largest or smallest values of a math function turns out to be a fundamentally difficult computational problem.

title: How Do New Organs Evolve? A Beetle Gland Shows the Way.
description: The evolution of a defensive gland in beetles shows how organs can arise from novel cells carving out new functional niches for their neighbors.

title: Physicists Create a Bizarre ‘Wigner Crystal’ Made Purely of Electrons
description: The unambiguous discovery of a Wigner crystal relied on a novel technique for probing the insides of complex materials.

title: Neither Star nor Planet: A Strange Brown Dwarf Puzzles Astronomers
description: Brown dwarfs such as “The Accident” are illuminating the murky borderlands that separate planets from stars.

title: Mating Contests Among Females, Long Ignored, May Shape Evolution
description: Showy male competitions over mating privileges have grabbed scientists’ attention more often, but new work hints that sexual selection is also widespread among females.

title: A Soil-Science Revolution Upends Plans to Fight Climate Change
description: A centuries-old concept in soil science has recently been thrown out. Yet it remains a key ingredient in everything from climate models to advanced carbon-capture projects.

title: How Bell’s Theorem Proved ‘Spooky Action at a Distance’ Is Real
description: The root of today’s quantum revolution was John Stewart Bell’s 1964 theorem showing that quantum mechanics really permits instantaneous connections between far-apart locations.

title: New Shape Opens ‘Wormhole’ Between Numbers and Geometry
description: Laurent Fargues and Peter Scholze have found a new, more powerful way of connecting number theory and geometry as part of the sweeping Langlands program.

title: A Video Tour of the Standard Model
description: The Standard Model is a sweeping equation that has correctly predicted the results of virtually every experiment ever conducted, as Quanta explores in a new video.

title: Mathematicians Prove Symmetry of Phase Transitions
description: A group of mathematicians has shown that at critical moments, a symmetry called rotational invariance is a universal property across many physical systems.

title: ‘Social’ Mitochondria, Whispering Between Cells, Influence Health
description: Mitochondria appear to communicate and cooperate with one another, both within and between cells. Biologists are only just beginning to understand how and why.

title: How ‘Long COVID’ Keeps Us Sick
description: Other diseases with long-term symptoms can help us understand how COVID can affect us long after the virus itself is gone.

title: A Lack of COVID-19 Genomes Could Prolong the Pandemic
description: Genomic surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 virus can help control the current pandemic and prevent future ones. But the process is marred by insufficient data and geographic inequities.

title: Same or Different? The Question Flummoxes Neural Networks.
description: For all their triumphs, AI systems can’t seem to generalize the concepts of “same” and “different.” Without that, researchers worry, the quest to create truly intelligent machines may be hopeless.

title: Gas Giants’ Energy Crisis Solved After 50 Years
description: Jupiter and Saturn should be freezing cold. Instead, they’re hot. Researchers now know why.

title: Mathematicians Prove 2D Version of Quantum Gravity Really Works
description: In three towering papers, a team of mathematicians has worked out the details of Liouville quantum field theory, a two-dimensional model of quantum gravity.

title: Graphene Superconductors May Be Less Exotic Than Physicists Hoped
description: Superconductivity has been discovered in graphene devices without any twists, suggesting the form of superconductivity in the material might be mundane after all.

title: RNA Brakes May Stabilize a Cellular Symbiosis
description: In some symbiotic partnerships, an RNA-based mechanism may sabotage the growth of greedy hosts.

title: A Burp or a Blast? Seismic Signals Reveal the Volcanic Eruption to Come
description: Scientists have begun to decipher the subtle signs that reveal how explosive a volcanic eruption is going to be.

title: A Number Theorist Who Connects Math to Other Creative Pursuits
description: Jordan Ellenberg enjoys studying — and writing about — the mathematics underlying everyday phenomena.

title: Squishy Neutron Star Setback Dampens Hopes of Exotic Matter
description: Groundbreaking results show that neutron stars of different masses may have the same size — upending astrophysical models.

title: Mathematicians Answer Old Question About Odd Graphs
description: A pair of mathematicians solved a legendary question about the proportion of vertices in a graph with an odd number of connections.

title: Eve Marder on the Crucial Resilience of Neurons
description: Eve Marder’s research into the plasticity and resilience of nervous systems finds universal principles guiding life’s responses to stress.

title: DNA’s Histone Spools Hint at How Complex Cells Evolved
description: New work shows that histones, long treated as boring spools for DNA, sit at the center of the origin story of eukaryotes and continue to play important roles in evolution and disease.

title: How Gravity Is a Double Copy of Other Forces
description: An enigmatic connection between the forces of nature is allowing physicists to explore gravity’s quantum side.

title: Researchers Read the Sugary ‘Language’ on Cell Surfaces
description: Glycans, the complex sugars that stud cellular surfaces, are like a language that life uses to mediate vital interactions. Researchers are learning how to read their meaning.

title: New Proof Reveals That Graphs With No Pentagons Are Fundamentally Different
description: Researchers have proved a special case of the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture, which shows what happens in graphs that exclude anything resembling a pentagon.

title: DNA of Giant ‘Corpse Flower’ Parasite Surprises Biologists
description: The bizarre genome of the world’s most mysterious flowering plants shows how far parasites will go in stealing, deleting and duplicating DNA.

title: Melanie Mitchell Takes AI Research Back to Its Roots
description: To build a general artificial intelligence, we may need to know more about our own minds, argues the computer scientist Melanie Mitchell.

title: Latest Neural Nets Solve World’s Hardest Equations Faster Than Ever Before
description: Two new approaches allow deep neural networks to solve entire families of partial differential equations, making it easier to model complicated systems and to do so orders of magnitude faster.

title: The Brain ‘Rotates’ Memories to Save Them From New Sensations
description: Some populations of neurons simultaneously process sensations and memories. New work shows how the brain rotates those representations to prevent interference.

title: How Radio Astronomy Reveals the Universe
description: Radio waves, longer and less energetic than visible light, give astronomers access to some of the most obscure physics in the cosmos.

title: Trachette Jackson Fights Cancer With Math
description: Quantitative models built by the mathematical biologist Trachette Jackson can make cancer therapies safer and more effective.

title: New Genomic Study of Placenta Finds Deep Links to Cancer
description: A patchwork of genomic differences in the placenta may explain the organ’s “live fast, die young” strategy and its connections to cancer.

title: ‘Last Hope’ Experiment Finds Evidence for Unknown Particles
description: Today’s long-anticipated announcement by Fermilab’s Muon g-2 team appears to solidify a tantalizing conflict between nature and theory. But a separate calculation, published at the same time, has clouded the picture.

title: Mathematicians Settle Erdős Coloring Conjecture
description: Fifty years ago, Paul Erdős and two other mathematicians came up with a graph theory problem that they thought they might solve on the spot. A team of mathematicians has finally settled it.

title: Cells Form Into ‘Xenobots’ on Their Own
description: Embryonic cells can self-assemble into new living forms that don’t resemble the bodies they usually generate, challenging old ideas of what defines an organism.

title: Scientists Pin Down When Earth’s Crust Cracked, Then Came to Life
description: New data indicating that Earth’s surface broke up about 3.2 billion years ago helps clarify how plate tectonics drove the evolution of complex life.

title: Sharon Glotzer’s Deep Curiosity About Order From Chaos
description: The computational physicist Sharon Glotzer finds unifying principles that structure the chaotic dance of the particles that make up matter.

title: Chasing the Elusive Numbers That Define Epidemics
description: Most modeling efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic have sought to address urgent practical concerns. But some groups aim to bolster the theoretical underpinnings of that work instead.

title: Why Extraterrestrial Life May Not Seem Entirely Alien
description: The zoologist Arik Kershenbaum argues that because some evolutionary challenges are truly universal, life throughout the cosmos may share certain features.

title: Pioneers Linking Math and Computer Science Win the Abel Prize
description: Avi Wigderson and László Lovász won for their work developing complexity theory and graph theory, respectively, and for connecting the two fields.

title: A New Twist Reveals Superconductivity’s Secrets
description: An unexpected superconductor was beginning to look like a fluke, but a new theory and a second discovery have revealed that emergent quasiparticles may be behind the effect.

title: Frank Wilczek on the Strong Force, Quarks and Dark Matter
description: The theoretical physicist Frank Wilczek explained what holds atomic nuclei together, and he is still pushing at the limits of what the standard model can tell us.

title: Quantum Mischief Rewrites the Laws of Cause and Effect
description: Spurred on by quantum experiments that scramble the ordering of causes and their effects, some physicists are figuring out how to abandon causality altogether.

title: Bonnie Bassler on Talkative Bacteria and Eavesdropping Viruses
description: The molecular biologist Bonnie Bassler is deciphering the chemical languages that bacteria use to coordinate their assaults on a host.

title: New Algorithm Breaks Speed Limit for Solving Linear Equations
description: By harnessing randomness, a new algorithm achieves a fundamentally novel — and faster — way of performing one of the most basic computations in math and computer science.

title: Isadore Singer Transcended Mathematical Boundaries
description: A former graduate student reflects on how Isadore Singer, who died on February 11, brought together mathematicians, physicists and anyone else interested in the deeper connections between diverse fields.

title: Neil Shubin on Tiktaalik , Ballistic Tongues and Evolution
description: The paleontologist Neil Shubin talks with host Steven Strogatz about hunting for a 375 million-year-old fossil and finding novel traits that evolved many times.

title: How to Understand COVID-19 Variants and Their Effects on Vaccines
description: Researchers are tracking the different strains of SARS-CoV-2 and studying how they spread through our population and our bodies.

title: Cloud-Making Aerosol Could Devastate Polar Sea Ice
description: An overlooked but powerful driver of cloud formation could accelerate the loss of polar sea ice.

title: Artificial Neural Nets Finally Yield Clues to How Brains Learn
description: The learning algorithm that enables the runaway success of deep neural networks doesn’t work in biological brains, but researchers are finding alternatives that could.

title: Some Proteins Change Their Folds to Perform Different Jobs
description: Unusual proteins that can quickly fold into different shapes provide cells with a novel regulatory mechanism.

title: Rumbles on Mars Raise Hopes of Underground Magma Flows
description: Small and cold, Mars has long been considered a dead planet. But a series of recent discoveries has forced scientists to rethink how recently its insides stopped churning — if they ever stopped at all.

title: The Hard Lessons of Modeling the Coronavirus Pandemic
description: In the fight against COVID-19, disease modelers have struggled against misunderstanding and misuse of their work. They have also come to realize how unready the state of modeling was for this pandemic.

title: ‘Unicorn’ Discovery Points to a New Population of Black Holes
description: Small black holes were nowhere to be found, leading astronomers to wonder if they didn’t exist at all. Now a series of findings, including a “unicorn” black hole, has raised hopes of solving the decade-long mystery.

title: Plant Cells of Different Species Can Swap Organelles
description: In grafted plants, shrunken chloroplasts can jump between species by slipping through unexpected gateways in cell walls.

title: Mathematicians Resurrect Hilbert’s 13th Problem
description: Long considered solved, David Hilbert’s question about seventh-degree polynomials is leading researchers to a new web of mathematical connections.

title: A Newfound Source of Cellular Order in the Chemistry of Life
description: Inside cells, droplets of biomolecules called condensates merge, divide and dissolve. Their dance may regulate vital processes.

title: The Year in Math and Computer Science
description: Even as mathematicians and computer scientists proved big results in computational complexity, number theory and geometry, computers proved themselves increasingly indispensable in mathematics.

title: The Mystery of Mistletoe’s Missing Genes
description: Mistletoes have all but shut down the powerhouses of their cells. Scientists are still trying to understand the plants’ unorthodox survival strategy.

title: How the Slowest Computer Programs Illuminate Math’s Fundamental Limits
description: The goal of the “busy beaver” game is to find the longest-running computer program. Its pursuit has surprising connections to some of the most profound questions and concepts in mathematics.

title: How Neutral Theory Altered Ideas About Biodiversity
description: The simple insight that most changes are random had a profound effect on genetics, evolution and ecology.

title: New Fish Data Reveal How Evolutionary Bursts Create Species
description: In three bursts of adaptive change, one species of cichlid fish in Lake Tanganyika gave rise to hundreds.

title: Undergraduate Math Student Pushes Frontier of Graph Theory
description: At 21, Ashwin Sah has produced a body of work that senior mathematicians say is nearly unprecedented for a college student.

title: Did Viruses Create the Nucleus? The Answer May Be Near.
description: An unorthodox symbiotic theory about the origin of eukaryotes’ defining characteristic may soon be put to the test.

title: How to Solve Our Three John Conway-Inspired Puzzles
description: A numerical puzzle, a geometric puzzle and a game of random patterns — all with connections to the legendary mathematician — elicited an enthusiastic response from readers.

title: Scientists Uncover the Universal Geometry of Geology
description: An exercise in pure mathematics has led to a wide-ranging theory of how the world comes together.

title: Scientists Find Vital Genes Evolving in Genome’s Junkyard
description: Even genes essential for life can be caught in an evolutionary arms race that forces them to change or be replaced.

title: Computer Scientists Achieve ‘Crown Jewel’ of Cryptography
description: A cryptographic master tool called indistinguishability obfuscation has for years seemed too good to be true. Three researchers have figured out that it can work.

title: Disorder Persists in Larger Graphs, New Math Proof Finds
description: David Conlon and Asaf Ferber have raised the lower bound for multicolor “Ramsey numbers,” which quantify how big graphs can get before patterns inevitably emerge.

title: Brain Cell DNA Refolds Itself to Aid Memory Recall
description: Researchers see structural changes in genetic material that allow memories to strengthen when remembered.

title: Deep Neural Networks Help to Explain Living Brains
description: Deep neural networks, often criticized as “black boxes,” are helping neuroscientists understand the organization of living brains.

title: To Boldly Go Where No Internet Protocol Has Gone Before
description: Vinton Cerf helped create the internet 40 years ago, and he’s still working to connect people around the world — and off it.

title: Celebrating the Playful Magic of John Horton Conway
description: Have fun exploring a numerical puzzle, a geometric puzzle and a game of random patterns, all inspired by the playful genius of the legendary mathematician.

title: A Physicist’s Approach to Biology Brings Ecological Insights
description: The physicist Jeff Gore tests theories about microbe communities experimentally and finds new rules governing ecological stability.

title: Scientists Win Nobel Prize for Discovering the Hepatitis C Virus
description: Harvey Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles Rice were awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discovery of the cause of a major liver disease.

title: Some Physicists See Signs of Cosmic Strings From the Big Bang
description: Subtle aberrations in the clockwork blinking of stars could become “the result of the century.” That’s if the distortions are produced by a network of giant filaments left over from the birth of the universe.

title: Complexity Scientist Beats Traffic Jams Through Adaptation
description: To tame urban traffic, the computer scientist Carlos Gershenson finds that letting transportation systems adapt and self-organize often works better than trying to predict and control them.

title: A New Algorithm for Graph Crossings, Hiding in Plain Sight
description: Two computer scientists found — in the unlikeliest of places — just the idea they needed to make a big leap in graph theory.

title: How Two Became One: Origins of a Mysterious Symbiosis Found
description: Carpenter ants need endosymbiotic bacteria to guide the early development of their embryos. New work has reconstructed how this deep partnership evolved.

title: An Unexpected Twist Lights Up the Secrets of Turbulence
description: Having solved a central mystery about the “twirliness” of tornadoes and other types of vortices, William Irvine has set his sights on turbulence, the white whale of classical physics.

title: By Losing Genes, Life Often Evolved More Complexity
description: Recent major surveys show that reductions in genomic complexity — including the loss of key genes — have successfully shaped the evolution of life throughout history.

title: How Close Are Computers to Automating Mathematical Reasoning?
description: AI tools are shaping next-generation theorem provers, and with them the relationship between math and machine.

title: Can Vaccines for Wildlife Prevent Human Pandemics?
description: Studies suggest that self-disseminating vaccines could prevent the "spillover" of animal viruses into humans as pandemic diseases.

title: Computer Search Settles 90-Year-Old Math Problem
description: By translating Keller’s conjecture into a computer-friendly search for a type of graph, researchers have finally resolved a problem about covering spaces with tiles.

title: Global Wave Discovery Ends 220-Year Search
description: An 18th-century physicist first predicted the existence of a chorus of atmospheric waves that swoop around Earth. Scientists have finally found them.

title: ‘Zombie’ Microbes Redefine Life’s Energy Limits
description: A new model shows that the denizens of a vast, ancient biome beneath the seafloor use barely enough energy to stay alive — and broadens understanding of what life can look like.

title: Mitochondria May Hold Keys to Anxiety and Mental Health
description: Research hints that the energy-generating organelles of cells may play a surprisingly pivotal role in mediating anxiety and depression.

title: How to Design (or at Least Model) Mixed Dog Breeds
description: Readers simulated the genetics of dog breeding to solve a puzzle about mixed breed percentages and sexual reproduction.

title: Why Are Plants Green? To Reduce the Noise in Photosynthesis.
description: Plants ignore the most energy-rich part of sunlight because stability matters more than efficiency, according to a new model of photosynthesis.

title: An Alternative to Dark Matter Passes Critical Test
description: Modified gravity theories have never been able to describe the universe’s first light. A new formulation does.

title: Our Genes May Explain Severity of COVID-19 and Other Infections
description: Researchers are examining the power of subtle genetic weaknesses in the immune system to affect the severity of infectious diseases, including COVID-19.

title: How the Bits of Quantum Gravity Can Buzz
description: New calculations show how hypothetical particles called gravitons would give rise to a special kind of noise.

title: How Earth’s Climate Changes Naturally (and Why Things Are Different Now)
description: Earth’s climate has fluctuated through deep time, pushed by these 10 different causes. Here’s how each compares with modern climate change.

title: How and Why Computers Roll Loaded Dice
description: Researchers are one step closer to injecting probability into deterministic machines.

title: Why Is Glass Rigid? Signs of Its Secret Structure Emerge.
description: At the molecular level, glass looks like a liquid. But an artificial neural network has picked up on hidden structure in its molecules that may explain why glass is rigid like a solid.

title: Cosmic Rays May Explain Life’s Bias for Right-Handed DNA
description: Cosmic rays may have given right-handed genetic helixes an evolutionary edge at the beginning of life’s history.

title: The Cartoon Picture of Magnets That Has Transformed Science
description: One hundred years after it was proposed, the Ising model is used to understand everything from magnets to brains.

title: Why South Asia’s COVID-19 Numbers Are So Low (For Now)
description: Many theories have been offered for why the official COVID-19 toll on the Indian subcontinent has been surprisingly low. The best explanation may be the shortage of good, timely data.

title: Dark Matter Experiment Finds Unexplained Signal
description: Researchers say there are three possible explanations for the anomalous data. One is mundane. Two would revolutionize physics.

title: Random Search Wired Into Animals May Help Them Hunt
description: The nervous systems of foraging and predatory animals may prompt them to move along a special kind of random path called a Lévy walk to find food efficiently when no clues are available.

title: A Digital Locksmith Has Decoded Biology’s Molecular Keys
description: Neural networks have been taught to quickly read the surfaces of proteins — molecules critical to many biological processes.

title: In a Single Measure, Invariants Capture the Essence of Math Objects
description: To distinguish between fundamentally different objects, mathematicians turn to invariants that encode the objects’ essential features.

title: Black Hole Paradoxes Reveal a Fundamental Link Between Energy and Order
description: By chewing on the problems posed by “extremal” black holes, physicists have exposed a surprising and universal connection between energy and entropy.

title: Spreading the Word on a Possible Alzheimer’s Treatment
description: Neuroscientists could use brain waves to spur immune cells into action against the disease — but the process is almost too fantastic to believe.

title: Growing Anomalies at the Large Hadron Collider Raise Hopes
description: Collider physicists report that several measurements of particles called B mesons deviate from predictions. Alone, each oddity looks like a fluke, but their collective drift is more suggestive.

title: Out-of-Sync ‘Loners’ May Secretly Protect Orderly Swarms
description: Studies of collective behavior usually focus on how crowds of organisms coordinate their actions. But what if the individuals that don’t participate have just as much to tell us?

title: Symbolic Mathematics Finally Yields to Neural Networks
description: After translating some of math’s complicated equations, researchers have created an AI system that they hope will answer even bigger questions.

title: Egg Laying or Live Birth: How Evolution Chooses
description: A lizard that both lays eggs and gives birth to live young is helping scientists understand how and why these forms of reproduction evolved.

title: Inside Deep Undersea Rocks, Life Thrives Without the Sun
description: Newly discovered worlds of microbes far beneath the ocean floor, inside old basaltic rocks, could point to a greater likelihood of life elsewhere in the universe.

title: What Goes On in a Proton? Quark Math Still Conflicts With Experiments.
description: Two ways of approximating the ultra-complicated math that governs quark particles have recently come into conflict, leaving physicists unsure what their decades-old theory predicts.

title: Sugary Camouflage on Coronavirus Offers Vaccine Clues
description: In the fight against viruses and other pathogens, scientists are looking beyond genes and proteins to the complex sugars, or glycans, on cell surfaces.

title: Common Sense Comes Closer to Computers
description: The problem of common-sense reasoning has plagued the field of artificial intelligence for over 50 years. Now a new approach, borrowing from two disparate lines of thinking, has made important progress.

title: Why Sex? Biologists Find New Explanations.
description: Why did sex evolve? Theories usually focus on the diversity of future generations, but some researchers find compelling explanations in the immediate benefits to individuals.

title: New Earthquake Math Predicts How Destructive They’ll Be
description: The “pinball” model of a slipping fault line borrows from the mathematics of avalanches.

title: Neutrino Asymmetry Passes Critical Threshold
description: The first official evidence of a key imbalance between neutrinos and antineutrinos provides one of the best clues for why the universe contains something rather than nothing.

title: Some Animals Have No Microbiome. Here’s What That Tells Us.
description: To stay healthy, humans and some other animals rely on a complex community of bacteria in their guts. But research is starting to show that those partnerships might be more the exception than the rule.

title: Moon Duchin on Fair Voting and Random Walks
description: Can geometry save democracy from gerrymandering? Mathematician Moon Duchin discusses the possibilities with host Steven Strogatz.

title: Does Time Really Flow? New Clues Come From a Century-Old Approach to Math.
description: The laws of physics imply that the passage of time is an illusion. To avoid this conclusion, we might have to rethink the reality of infinitely precise numbers.

title: ‘Amazing’ Math Bridge Extended Beyond Fermat’s Last Theorem
description: Mathematicians have figured out how to expand the reach of a mysterious bridge connecting two distant continents in the mathematical world.

title: Billion-Year-Old Algae and Newer Genes Hint at Land Plants’ Origin
description: A recently unearthed fossil and new genomic discoveries are filling important gaps in scientists’ understanding of how primitive green algae eventually evolved into land vegetation.

title: A Rapid End Strikes the Dinosaur Extinction Debate
description: The paleontologist Pincelli Hull has nailed down the timing and speed of the extinction that killed off the dinosaurs — details that carry ominous warnings for today.

title: Nature Versus Nurture? Add ‘Noise’ to the Debate.
description: We give our genes and our environment all the credit for making us who we are. But random noise during development might be just as important.

title: Sudden Ancient Global Warming Event Traced to Magma Flood
description: A study has cemented the link between an intense global warming episode 56 million years ago and volcanism in the North Atlantic, with implications for modern climate change.

title: Cori Bargmann on the Genetics of Transparent Worms, Supertasters and Cancer
description: The neurogenetics pioneer Cori Bargmann speaks with host Steven Strogatz about why a transparent worm became her favorite animal and how a genetic discovery she made inspired a revolutionary cancer treatment.

title: Cryptography Pioneer Seeks Secure Elections the Low-Tech Way
description: Ronald Rivest helped come up with the RSA algorithm, which safeguards online commerce. Now he’s hoping to make democratic elections more trustworthy.

title: Ideal Glass Would Explain Why Glass Exists at All
description: Glass is anything that’s rigid like a crystal, yet made of disordered molecules like a liquid. To understand why it exists, researchers are attempting to create the perfect, still-hypothetical “ideal glass.”

title: Machine Learning Takes On Antibiotic Resistance
description: To combat resistant bacteria and refill the trickling antibiotic pipeline, scientists are getting help from deep learning networks.

title: Biodiversity May Thrive Through Games of Rock-Paper-Scissors
description: Recent findings add weight to the evidence that the intransitive competitions between species enrich the diversity of nature.

title: Landmark Computer Science Proof Cascades Through Physics and Math
description: Computer scientists established a new boundary on computationally verifiable knowledge. In doing so, they solved major open problems in quantum mechanics and pure mathematics.

title: Wormholes Reveal a Way to Manipulate Black Hole Information in the Lab
description: A proposal for building wormhole-connected black holes offers a way to probe the paradoxes of quantum information.

title: John Urschel: From NFL Player to Mathematician
description: John Urschel, who retired from playing professional football with the Baltimore Ravens to become a mathematician, talks to host Steven Strogatz about the fascinations of graph theory that lured him away from the NFL.

title: The Animal Origins of Coronavirus and Flu
description: Zoonotic diseases like influenza and many coronaviruses start out in animals, but their biological machinery often enables them to jump to humans.

title: In Brain Waves, Scientists See Neurons Juggle Possible Futures
description: Faced with a decision, the brain weighs its options by bundling them into rapidly alternating cycles of brain waves.

title: Rainbow Proof Shows Graphs Have Uniform Parts
description: Mathematicians have proved that copies of smaller graphs can always be used to perfectly cover larger ones.

title: Corina Tarnita and the Deep Mathematics of Social Insects
description: The mathematical biologist Corina Tarnita explains to host Steven Strogatz how quantitative modeling solved the mystery of fairy circles.

title: Immune Cell Assassins Reveal Their Nurturing Side
description: Don’t be misled by the bloodthirsty names of immune cells. Mounting research shows that the cells also fine-tune tissues and help the body heal.

title: The Grand Unified Theory of Rogue Waves
description: Rogue waves — enigmatic giants of the sea — were thought to be caused by two different mechanisms. But a new idea that borrows from the hinterlands of probability theory has the potential to predict them all.

title: Mathematicians Prove Universal Law of Turbulence
description: By exploiting randomness, three mathematicians have proved an elegant law that underlies the chaotic motion of turbulent systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Will Do What We Ask. That’s a Problem.
description: By teaching machines to understand our true desires, one scientist hopes to avoid the potentially disastrous consequences of having them do what we command.

title: How Ancient Light Reveals the Universe’s Contents
description: A photograph of the infant cosmos reveals the precise amounts of dark matter and dark energy in the universe, leaving precious little room for argument.

title: Glial Brain Cells, Long in Neurons’ Shadow, Reveal Hidden Powers
description: The glial cells of the nervous system have been eclipsed in importance by neurons for decades. But glia are turning out to be central to many neurological functions, including pain perception.

title: How Pi Connects Colliding Blocks to a Quantum Search Algorithm
description: A curious physicist has discovered an unexpected link between theoretical block collisions and a famed quantum search algorithm.

title: The Voyage to the End of Ice
description: Summer sea ice could vanish later this decade, with disastrous consequences. It all depends on the physics of ice.

title: Hidden Computational Power Found in the Arms of Neurons
description: The dendritic arms of some human neurons can perform logic operations that once seemed to require whole neural networks.

title: For Fluid Equations, a Steady Flow of Progress
description: A startling experimental discovery about how fluids behave started a wave of important mathematical proofs.

title: An Idea From Physics Helps AI See in Higher Dimensions
description: The laws of physics stay the same no matter one’s perspective. Now this idea is allowing computers to detect features in curved and higher-dimensional space.

title: How Simple Math Can Cover Even the Most Complex Holes
description: No one knows how to find the smallest shape that can cover all other shapes of a certain width. But high school geometry is getting us closer to an answer.

title: Continents of the Underworld Come Into Focus
description: Giant blobs nestled deep in the Earth may influence everything from the structure of island chains to mass-extinction events.

title: Biodiversity Alters Strategies of Bacterial Evolution
description: In evolution, context is everything: Bacteria with neighbors evolve to rebuff viruses in a different way.

title: Unscrambled Eggs: Self-Organization Restores Cells’ Order
description: To scientists’ surprise, blended mixtures of cytoplasm can reorganize themselves into cell-like compartments with working structural components.

title: The Year in Physics
description: Physicists saw a black hole for the first time, debated the expansion rate of the universe, pondered the origin of time and modeled the end of clouds.

title: The Year in Biology
description: Researchers explored the zone between life and death, charted the mind’s system for arranging ideas and memories and learned how life’s complexity emerged.

title: The Year in Math and Computer Science
description: Mathematicians and computer scientists made big progress in number theory, graph theory, machine learning and quantum computing, even as they reexamined our fundamental understanding of mathematics and neural networks.

title: Famous Fluid Equations Spring a Leak
description: Researchers have spent centuries looking for a scenario in which the Euler fluid equations fail. Now a mathematician has finally found one.

title: Sleeping Brain Waves Draw a Healthy Bath for Neurons
description: An organized tide of brain waves, blood and spinal fluid pulsing through a sleeping brain may flush away neural toxins that cause Alzheimer’s and other diseases.

title: To Decode the Brain, Scientists Automate the Study of Behavior
description: Machine learning and deep neural networks can capture and analyze the “language” of animal behavior in ways that go beyond what’s humanly possible.

title: How to Permanently End Diseases
description: Smallpox was eradicated relatively quickly, but other diseases have proved harder to eliminate. The reasons are a mix of biology and psychology.

title: Longevity Linked to Proteins That Calm Overexcited Neurons
description: New research makes a molecular connection between the brain and aging — and shows that overactive neurons can shorten life span.

title: Solution: ‘Randomness From Determinism’
description: Readers’ modifications of a bean machine showed how deterministic laws are capable of producing random-seeming behavior.

title: Playing Hide-and-Seek, Machines Invent New Tools
description: After millions of games, machine learning algorithms found creative solutions and unexpected new strategies that could transfer to the real world.

title: Cells That ‘Taste’ Danger Set Off Immune Responses
description: Taste and smell receptors in unexpected organs monitor the state of the body’s natural microbial health and raise an alarm over invading parasites.

title: Mathematicians Calculate How Randomness Creeps In
description: Mathematicians have figured out exactly how many moves it takes to randomize a 15 puzzle.

title: Computers Evolve a New Path Toward Human Intelligence
description: By ignoring their goals, evolutionary algorithms have solved longstanding challenges in artificial intelligence.

title: Dueling Brain Waves Anchor or Erase Learning During Sleep
description: While we sleep, one kind of slow brain wave helps to reinforce memories, but a competing wave weakens them.

title: Mathematicians Begin to Tame Wild ‘Sunflower’ Problem
description: A major advance toward solving the 60-year-old sunflower conjecture is shedding light on how order begins to appear as random systems grow in size.

title: Machines Beat Humans on a Reading Test. But Do They Understand?
description: A tool known as BERT can now beat humans on advanced reading-comprehension tests. But it's also revealed how far AI has to go.

title: How Randomness Can Arise From Determinism
description: Playing with a simple bean machine illustrates how deterministic laws can produce probabilistic, random-seeming behavior.

title: Nobel Prize Awarded for Discoveries on How Cells Adapt to Oxygen
description: The 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honored William Kaelin Jr., Peter Ratcliffe and Gregg Semenza for their work on elucidating how cells adjust to low oxygen levels.

title: Cell-Bacteria Mergers Offer Clues to How Organelles Evolved
description: Cells in symbiotic partnership, sometimes nested one within the other and functioning like organelles, can borrow from their host’s genes to complete their own metabolic pathways.

title: How Jurassic Plankton Stole Control of the Ocean’s Chemistry
description: Only 170 million years ago, new plankton evolved. Their demand for carbon and calcium permanently transformed the seas as homes for life.

title: Solution: ‘Perfect Randomness’
description: Is nature inherently random or is perfect randomness just an illusion based on our ignorance?

title: Artificial Intelligence Takes On Earthquake Prediction
description: After successfully predicting laboratory earthquakes, a team of geophysicists has applied a machine learning algorithm to quakes in the Pacific Northwest.

title: Math Reveals the Secrets of Cells’ Feedback Circuitry
description: Maintaining perfect stability through negative feedback is a basic element of electrical circuitry, but it’s been a mystery how cells could do it — until now.

title: New Hybrid Species Remix Old Genes Creatively
description: Clues from fish diversity suggest that interbreeding between species could be a major mechanism of fast speciation.

title: Where Quantum Probability Comes From
description: There are many different ways to think about probability. Quantum mechanics embodies them all.

title: Bacterial Clones Show Surprising Individuality
description: Genetically identical bacteria should all be the same, but in fact, the cells are stubbornly varied individuals.

title: Fossil DNA Reveals New Twists in Modern Human Origins
description: Modern humans and more ancient hominins interbred many times throughout Eurasia and Africa, and the genetic flow went both ways.

title: Soil’s Microbial Market Shows the Ruthless Side of Forests
description: In the “underground economy” for soil nutrients, fungi strike hard bargains and punish plants that won’t meet their price.

title: The Anthropologist of Artificial Intelligence
description: Iyad Rahwan’s radical idea: The best way to understand algorithms is to observe their behavior in the wild.

title: A Mathematical Model Unlocks the Secrets of Vision
description: Mathematicians and neuroscientists have created the first anatomically accurate model that explains how vision is possible.

title: The Puzzling Search for Perfect Randomness
description: Does objective, perfect randomness exist, or is randomness merely a product of our ignorance?

title: To Make Two Black Holes Collide, Try Three
description: How do black holes merge and make gravitational waves? Maybe with a little help from their friends.

title: For Embryo’s Cells, Size Can Determine Fate
description: Modeling suggests that many embryonic cells commit to a developmental fate when they become too small to divide unevenly anymore.

title: Unexpected ‘Germline’ Plant Cells May Shield New Generations
description: To avoid passing on new mutations to offspring, plants may minimize the number of divisions by the stem cells that make flowers and seeds.

title: Sun’s Puzzling Plasma Recreated in a Laboratory
description: For the first time, researchers have created a scale model of the twisting loops of the sun’s magnetic field.

title: Solution: Magic Moiré in Twisted Graphene
