description: Answering these simple questions can give you an intuitive feel for the geometric properties behind the emergence of superconductivity in rotated graphene sheets.

title: His Artificial Intelligence Sees Inside Living Cells
description: The computer vision scientist Greg Johnson is building systems that can recognize organelles on sight and show the dynamics of living cells more clearly than microscopy can.

title: Scientists Debate the Origin of Cell Types in the First Animals
description: Theories about how animals became multicellular are shifting as researchers find greater complexity in our single-celled ancestors.

title: How Swarming Insects Act Like Fluids
description: By studying a swarm of flying midges as though it were a fluid, physicists have learned how collective behaviors might stabilize a group against environmental disruptions.

title: How Randomness Can Make Math Easier
description: Randomness would seem to make a mathematical statement harder to prove. In fact, it often does the opposite.

title: Cellular Life, Death and Everything in Between
description: The discovery that apparently dead cells can sometimes resurrect themselves has researchers exploring how far they can push the point of no return.

title: The Quantum Theory That Peels Away the Mystery of Measurement
description: A recent test has confirmed the predictions of quantum trajectory theory.

title: Random Surfaces Hide an Intricate Order
description: Mathematicians have proved that a random process applied to a random surface will yield consistent patterns.

title: Where We See Shapes, AI Sees Textures
description: To researchers’ surprise, deep learning vision algorithms often fail at classifying images because they mostly take cues from textures, not shapes.

title: Philosophers Debate New ‘Sonic Black Hole’ Discovery
description: Opinions differ about what recent measurements of a sound-trapping fluid reveal about light-trapping black holes.

title: What’s in a Name? Taxonomy Problems Vex Biologists
description: Researchers struggle to incorporate ongoing evolutionary discoveries into an animal classification scheme older than Darwin.

title: When Magic Is Seen in Twisted Graphene, That’s a Moiré
description: What do moiré patterns seen in optics, art, photography and color printing have to do with superconducting layers of graphene?

title: How to Turn a Quantum Computer Into the Ultimate Randomness Generator
description: Pure, verifiable randomness is hard to come by. Two proposals show how to make quantum computers into randomness factories.

title: A 53-Year-Old Network Coloring Conjecture Is Disproved
description: In just three pages, a Russian mathematician has presented a better way to color certain types of networks than many experts thought possible.

title: Bacterial Complexity Revises Ideas About ‘Which Came First?’
description: Contrary to popular belief, bacteria have organelles too. Scientists are now studying them for insights into how complex cells evolved.

title: A Close Look at Newborn Planets Reveals Hints of Infant Moons
description: Astronomers have discovered a complex planetary system still swirling into existence.

title: Do Brains Operate at a Tipping Point? New Clues and Complications
description: New experimental results simultaneously advance and challenge the theory that the brain’s network of neurons balances on the knife-edge between two phases.

title: Immune Cells Measure Time to Identify Foreign Proteins
description: Immunologists confirm an old hunch: T-cells identify what belongs in the body by timing how long they can bind to it.

title: What’s the Magic Behind Graphene’s ‘Magic’ Angle?
description: A new theoretical model may help explain the shocking onset of superconductivity in stacked, twisted carbon sheets.

title: How Geometry, Data and Neighbors Predict Your Favorite Movies
description: A little high school geometry can help you understand the basic math behind movie recommendation engines.

title: Viruses Can Scatter Their Genes Among Cells and Reassemble
description: Some viruses can replicate without infecting any one cell with all their genes.

title: As Planet Discoveries Pile Up, a Gap Appears in the Pattern
description: Astronomers are puzzling over a paucity of planets in the galaxy measuring between 1.5 and two times Earth's size.

title: In Ecology Studies and Selfless Ants, He Finds Hope for the Future
description: For more than six decades, the influential biologist Edward O. Wilson has drawn connections between evolution, ecology and behavior, often sparking controversies inside and outside of science.

title: How Feynman Diagrams Revolutionized Physics
description: In the late 1940s, Richard Feynman invented a visual tool for simplifying particle calculations that forever changed theoretical physics.

title: Universal Pattern Explains Why Materials Conduct
description: Mathematicians have found that materials conduct electricity when electrons follow a universal mathematical pattern.

title: Brains Speed Up Perception by Guessing What’s Next
description: Your expectations shape and quicken your perceptions. A new model that explains how that happens also suggests it’s time to update theories about sensory perception and decision making.

title: With a Simple Twist, a ‘Magic’ Material Is Now the Big Thing in Physics
description: The stunning emergence of a new type of superconductivity with the mere twist of a carbon sheet has left physicists giddy, and its discoverer nearly overwhelmed.

title: Scientists Discover Nearly 200,000 Kinds of Ocean Viruses
description: New work raises the estimated diversity of viruses in the seas more than twelvefold and lays the groundwork for a better understanding of their impact on global nutrient cycles.

title: New Turmoil Over Predicting the Effects of Genes
description: Promising efforts at disentangling the effects of genes and the environment on complicated traits may have been confounded by statistical problems.

title: Icefish Study Adds Another Color to the Story of Blood
description: The rainbow of pigments that animals use for blood illustrates a central truth of evolution.

title: The Astronomer Who’d Rather Build Space Cameras
description: Jim Gunn shaped the theory of the evolution of the cosmos before building cameras and spectrographs for major observatories like the Hubble Space Telescope.

title: Heat-Loving Microbes, Once Dormant, Thrive Over Decades-Old Fire
description: In harsh ecosystems around the world, microbiologists are finding evidence that “microbial seed banks” protect biodiversity from changing conditions.

title: What the Sight of a Black Hole Means to a Black Hole Physicist
description: The astrophysicist Janna Levin reflects on the newly unveiled, first-ever photograph of a black hole.

title: Researchers Rethink the Ancestry of Complex Cells
description: New studies revise ideas about the symbiosis that gave mitochondria to cells and about whether the last common ancestor of all eukaryotes was one cell or many.

title: Scientists Discover Exotic New Patterns of Synchronization
description: In a world seemingly filled with chaos, physicists have discovered new forms of synchronization and are learning how to predict and control them.

title: Cryptography That Is Provably Secure
description: Researchers have just released hacker-proof cryptographic code — programs with the same level of invincibility as a mathematical proof.

title: Proof Finds That All Change Is a Mix of Order and Randomness
description: All descriptions of change are a unique blend of chance and determinism, according to the sweeping mathematical proof of the “weak Pinsker conjecture.”

title: Solution: ‘How to Find Simple Treasures in Complex Numbers’
description: Puzzle solvers used “imaginary” numbers to solve a real world problem: finding long-lost treasure.

title: She Finds Clues to Future Sustainability in Old Food Webs
description: By reconstructing prehistoric food webs and analyzing the diverse interactions of humans with other species, the ecologist Jennifer Dunne is developing a new understanding of sustainability through network science.

title: Quantum Machine Appears to Defy Universe’s Push for Disorder
description: One of the first quantum simulators has produced a puzzling phenomenon: a row of atoms that repeatedly pops back into place.

title: Biologists Discover Unknown Powers in Mighty Mitochondria
description: Mitochondria are most famous as sources of metabolic energy. But by splitting and combining, they can also release chemical signals to regulate cell activities, including the generation of neurons.

title: Where Proof, Evidence and Imagination Intersect
description: In mathematics, where proofs are everything, evidence is important too. But evidence is only as good as the model, and modeling can be dangerous business. So how much evidence is enough?

title: The Math That Tells Cells What They Are
description: During development, cells seem to decode their fate through optimal information processing, which could hint at a more general principle of life.

title: How Artificial Intelligence Is Changing Science
description: The latest AI algorithms are probing the evolution of galaxies, calculating quantum wave functions, discovering new chemical compounds and more. Is there anything that scientists do that can’t be automated?

title: The Universe’s Ultimate Complexity Revealed by Simple Quantum Games
description: A two-player game can reveal whether the universe has an infinite amount of complexity.

title: Smarter Parts Make Collective Systems Too Stubborn
description: As researchers delve deeper into the behavior of decentralized collective systems, they’re beginning to question some of their initial assumptions.

title: A World Without Clouds
description: A state-of-the-art supercomputer simulation indicates that a feedback loop between global warming and cloud loss can push Earth’s climate past a disastrous tipping point in as little as a century.

title: How Our Universe Could Emerge as a Hologram
description: Physicists have devised a holographic model of “de Sitter space,” the term for a universe like ours, that could give us new clues about the origin of space and time.

title: New Squid Genome Shines Light on Symbiotic Evolution
description: Researchers hope that the genes of a glowing squid can illuminate how animals evolved organs for beneficial bacteria.

title: How to Find Simple Treasures in Complex Numbers
description: In spite of their name, “imaginary” numbers are as real as any other numbers, especially when it comes to hunting for lost treasure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Finds Ancient ‘Ghosts’ in Modern DNA
description: With the help of deep learning techniques, paleoanthropologists find evidence of long-lost branches on the human family tree.

title: How a Strange Grid Reveals Hidden Connections Between Simple Numbers
description: A graduate student has helped illuminate a long-suspected connection between addition and multiplication.

title: Fragile DNA Enables New Adaptations to Evolve Quickly
description: If highly repetitive gene-regulating sequences in DNA are easily lost, that may explain why some adaptations evolve quickly and repeatedly.

title: An Astrophysicist Who Maps the Universe’s Terra Incognita
description: Priyamvada Natarajan has pioneered the mapping and modeling of the universe’s invisible contents, especially dark matter and supermassive black holes.

title: Foundations Built for a General Theory of Neural Networks
description: Neural networks can be as unpredictable as they are powerful. Now mathematicians are beginning to reveal how a neural network’s form will influence its function.

title: Why Evolution Reversed These Insects’ Sex Organs
description: Among these cave insects, the females evolved to have penises — twice. The reasons challenge common assumptions about sex.

title: The Trouble With Turbulence
description: Turbulence is everywhere, yet it is one of the most difficult concepts for physicists to understand.

title: A Movement to Close the Gender Gap in Mathematics
description: The Brazilian mathematician Carolina Araujo, who calls herself “a bit of an anarchist,” is organizing meetings and building a support network to study and solve the problems women face in mathematics.

title: A New Approach to Understanding How Machines Think
description: Neural networks are famously incomprehensible, so Been Kim is developing a “translator for humans.”

title: Jellyfish Genome Hints That Complexity Isn’t Genetically Complex
description: Jellyfish didn’t need novel genes to take an evolutionary leap in complexity.

title: The Year in Biology
description: Biologists gained new insights into life’s genomically tumultuous past, viruses as crucial components of life, the hidden talents of complex cells and basic aspects of cognition and memory.

title: How Complex Wholes Emerge From Simple Parts
description: Throughout nature, throngs of relatively simple elements can self-organize into behaviors that seem unexpectedly complex. Scientists are beginning to understand why and how these phenomena emerge without a central organizing entity.

title: New Studies Rescue Gravitational-Wave Signal From the Noise
description: Two independent papers vanquish lingering doubts about LIGO’s historic discovery of gravitational waves.

title: What Defines a Stem Cell? Scientists Rethink the Answer
description: As it becomes clear that the body’s cells have more diverse regenerative capabilities than expected, experts have had to reconsider their approach to stem cell research.

title: Mathematical Simplicity May Drive Evolution’s Speed
description: Some researchers are using a complexity framework thought to be purely theoretical to understand evolutionary dynamics in biological and computational systems.

title: A Universal Law for the ‘Blood of the Earth’
description: Simple physical principles can be used to describe how rivers grow everywhere from Florida to Mars.

title: ‘Lava-Lamp’ Proteins May Help Cells Cheat Death
description: With proteins that reversibly self-assemble into droplets, cells may control their metabolism — and harden themselves against harsh conditions.

title: Should Evolution Treat Our Microbes as Part of Us?
description: How does evolution select the fittest “individuals” when they are ecosystems made up of hosts and their microbiomes? Biologist debate the need to revise theories.

title: How Holography Could Help Solve Quantum Gravity
description: In the latest campaign to reconcile Einstein’s theory of gravity with quantum mechanics, many physicists are studying how a higher dimensional space that includes gravity arises like a hologram from a lower dimensional particle theory.

title: Stem Cells Remember Tissues’ Past Injuries
description: Stem cells seem to retain memories of old injuries to improve future healing. When that system goes wrong, chronic inflammation can result.

title: Solution: ‘How Equality and Inequality Shape Birds and Bees’
description: Puzzle solvers explored how evolution may have used negative and positive control mechanisms to shape the conflicting parental functions of reproduction and child rearing.

title: Theorists Debate How ‘Neutral’ Evolution Really Is
description: For 50 years, evolutionary theory has emphasized the importance of neutral mutations rather than adaptive ones at the level of DNA. Real genomic data challenges that assumption.

title: In the Nucleus, Genes’ Activity Might Depend on Their Location
description: Using a new CRISPR-based technique, researchers are examining how the position of DNA within the nucleus affects gene expression and cell function.

title: Without a Proof, Mathematicians Wonder How Much Evidence Is Enough
description: A new statistical model appears to undermine long-held assumptions in number theory. How much should it be trusted when all that really matters is proof?

title: The (Imaginary) Numbers at the Edge of Reality
description: Odd enough to potentially model the strangeness of the physical world, complex numbers with “imaginary” components are rooted in the familiar.

title: Prepping for a Flood of Heavenly Bodies
description: Mario Jurić is leading the push to get astronomy ready for the torrents of data that are about to flow.

title: How Equality and Inequality Shape the Birds and the Bees
description: Two dynamic, seemingly opposing forces likely played an important role in the evolution of reproduction and child rearing in social animals like bees and humans.

title: ‘Broadband’ Networks of Viruses May Help Bacteria Evolve Faster
description: A newly discovered mechanism may enable viruses to shuttle genes between bacteria 1,000 times as often as was thought — making them a major force in those cells’ evolution.

title: In the Ticking of the Embryonic Clock, She Finds Answers
description: Renee Reijo Pera has spent decades uncovering how the timing of embryonic development contributes to health and disease.

title: Famous Experiment Dooms Alternative to Quantum Weirdness
description: Oil droplets guided by “pilot waves” have failed to reproduce the results of the quantum double-slit experiment, crushing a century-old dream that there exists a single, concrete reality.

title: Forests Emerge as a Major Overlooked Climate Factor
description: New work at the intersection of atmospheric science and ecology is finding that forests can influence rainfall and climate from across a continent.

title: Three Biochemists Win Chemistry Nobel for Directing Evolution
description: By using the power of evolution to solve practical problems, three researchers opened new avenues to chemical discovery.

title: Unexpected Diversity Found in 16 New Lab Mouse Genomes
description: The availability of 16 new mouse genomes will help accelerate research into the genetic underpinnings of human traits and diseases.

title: ‘Traffic Jams’ of Cells Help to Sculpt Embryos
description: By measuring mechanical forces inside an embryo for the first time, researchers have shown how a physical “jamming” mechanism assists development.

title: How Nature Defies Math in Keeping Ecosystems Stable
description: Paradoxically, the abundance of tight interactions among living species usually leads to disasters in ecological models. New analyses hint at how nature seemingly defies the math.

title: Machine Learning Confronts the Elephant in the Room
description: A visual prank exposes an Achilles’ heel of computer vision systems: Unlike humans, they can’t do a double take.

title: New AI Strategy Mimics How Brains Learn to Smell
description: Machine learning techniques are commonly based on how the visual system processes information. To beat their limitations, scientists are drawing inspiration from the sense of smell.

title: On Waste Plastics at Sea, She Finds Unique Microbial Multitudes
description: Maria-Luiza Pedrotti is illuminating the unseen worlds of plastic-eating bacteria that teem in massive ocean garbage patches.

title: A New Test for the Leading Big Bang Theory
description: Cosmologists have predicted the existence of an oscillating signal that could distinguish between cosmic inflation and alternative theories of the universe’s birth.

title: Solution: ‘Evolutionary Math and Just-So Stories’
description: How much stock should we put in mathematical models of evolution that have not been validated by rigorous empirical data?

title: Tinkertoy Models Produce New Geometric Insights
description: An upstart field that simplifies complex shapes is letting mathematicians understand how those shapes depend on the space in which you visualize them.

title: DNA Analysis Reveals a Genus of Plants Hiding in Plain Sight
description: Gene-sequence data is changing the way that botanists think about their classification schemes. A recent name-change for a common houseplant resulted from the discovery that it belonged in an overlooked genus.

title: To Heal Some Wounds, Adult Cells Turn More Fetal
description: Once again, body cells reveal unexpected plasticity: In a newly discovered type of wound healing, which some researchers call “paligenosis,” adult cells revert to a more fetal state.

title: To Understand Volcanoes on Other Worlds, Stand On Our Own
description: Rosaly Lopes has visited dozens of active volcanoes on Earth and discovered even more elsewhere in the solar system. Her work is helping to establish whether volcanoes on distant moons could create conditions friendly to life.

title: How Network Math Can Help You Make Friends
description: Studying the structure of existing friendships in your community can help you forge the best connections when forming a new circle of friends.

title: ‘Functional Fingerprint’ May Identify Brains Over a Lifetime
description: A unique neurological “functional fingerprint” allows scientists to explore the influence of genetics, environment and aging on brain connectivity.

title: Evolutionary Math and Just-So Stories
description: Evolutionary stories like the grandmother hypothesis are easy to construct from mathematical models, but how well do they reflect reality?

title: How Insulin Helped Create Ant Societies
description: Evolution may have coopted an ancient metabolic mechanism to set social insects on the path toward one of the most puzzling behaviors found in nature.

title: Universal Method to Sort Complex Information Found
description: The nearest neighbor problem asks where a new point fits into an existing data set. A few researchers set out to prove that there was no universal way to solve it. Instead, they found such a way.

title: A Poet of Computation Who Uncovers Distant Truths
description: The theoretical computer scientist Constantinos Daskalakis has won the Rolf Nevanlinna Prize for explicating core questions in game theory and machine learning.

title: A Master of Numbers and Shapes Who Is Rewriting Arithmetic
description: The 30-year-old math sensation Peter Scholze is now one of the youngest Fields medalists for “the revolution that he launched in arithmetic geometry.”

title: An Innovator Who Brings Order to an Infinitude of Equations
description: The mathematician Caucher Birkar was born on a subsistence farm and raised in the middle of the brutal war between Iran and Iraq. After fleeing to England, he has gone on to impose order on a wild landscape of mathematical equations.

title: A Traveler Who Finds Stability in the Natural World
description: The mathematician Alessio Figalli is rarely in one place for very long. But his work has established the stability of everything from crystals to weather fronts by using concepts derived from Napoleonic fortifications.

title: Swarming Bacteria Create an ‘Impossible’ Superfluid
description: Researchers explore a loophole that extracts useful energy from a fluid’s seemingly random motion. The secret? Sugar and asymmetry.

title: How Artificial Intelligence Can Supercharge the Search for New Particles
description: In the hunt for new fundamental particles, physicists have always had to make assumptions about how the particles will behave. New machine learning algorithms don’t.

title: Three Major Physics Discoveries and Counting
description: Sau Lan Wu spent decades working to establish the Standard Model of particle physics. Now she’s searching for what lies beyond it.

title: Why Nature Prefers Couples, Even for Yeast
description: Some species have the equivalent of many more than two sexes, but most do not. A new model suggests the reason depends on how often they mate.

title: A Short Guide to Hard Problems
description: What’s easy for a computer to do, and what’s almost impossible? Those questions form the core of computational complexity. We present a map of the landscape.

title: The Hunt for Earth’s Deep Hidden Oceans
description: Water-bearing minerals reveal that Earth’s mantle could hold more water than all its oceans. Researchers now ask: Where did it all come from?

title: To Make Sense of the Present, Brains May Predict the Future
description: A controversial theory suggests that perception, motor control, memory and other brain functions all depend on comparisons between ongoing actual experiences and the brain’s modeled expectations.

title: What Is the Sun Made Of and When Will It Die?
description: If and when physicists are able to pin down the metal content of the sun, that number could upend much of what we thought we knew about the evolution and life span of stars.

title: Mathematicians Tame Turbulence in Flattened Fluids
description: By squeezing fluids into flat sheets, researchers can get a handle on the strange ways that turbulence feeds energy into a system instead of eating it away.

title: Mathematics Shows How to Ensure Evolution
description: New results emerging from graph theory prove that the way a population is organized can guarantee the eventual triumph of natural selection — or permanently thwart it.

title: Finally, a Problem That Only Quantum Computers Will Ever Be Able to Solve
description: Computer scientists have been searching for years for a type of problem that a quantum computer can solve but that any possible future classical computer cannot. Now they’ve found one.

title: Theory Suggests That All Genes Affect Every Complex Trait
description: The more closely geneticists look at complex traits and diseases, the harder it gets to find active genes that don’t play some part in them.

title: Her Key to Modeling Brains: Ignore the Right Details
description: Being able to think like a physicist helps Carina Curto, a mathematician-turned-neuroscientist, pull insights about the human brain out of theoretical models.

title: Brains May Teeter Near Their Tipping Point
description: In a renewed attempt at a grand unified theory of brain function, physicists now argue that brains optimize performance by staying near — though not exactly at — the critical point between two phases.

title: The Physics of Glass Opens a Window Into Biology
description: The physicist Lisa Manning studies the dynamics of glassy materials to understand embryonic development and disease.

title: Why Earth’s Cracked Crust May Be Essential for Life
description: Life needs more than water alone. Recent discoveries suggest that plate tectonics has played a critical role in nourishing life on Earth. The findings carry major consequences for the search for life elsewhere in the universe.

title: There Are No Laws of Physics. There’s Only the Landscape.
description: Scientists seek a single description of reality. But modern physics allows for many different descriptions, many equivalent to one another, connected through a vast landscape of mathematical possibility.

title: Evidence Found for a New Fundamental Particle
description: An experiment at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory near Chicago has detected far more electron neutrinos than predicted — a possible harbinger of a revolutionary new elementary particle called the sterile neutrino, though many physicists remain skeptical.

title: Cores From Coral Reefs Hold Secrets of the Seas’ Past and Future
description: Layered deposits of coral skeletons hold vast stores of environmental data from thousands of years ago, including annual records of ocean temperatures, water pollution and storm activity.

title: How Brain Waves Surf Sound Waves to Process Speech
description: By paying more attention to behaviors, and not just the activity of neurons, two researchers critical of most neuroscience learned how brains make sense of spoken language.

title: To Build Truly Intelligent Machines, Teach Them Cause and Effect
description: Judea Pearl, a pioneering figure in artificial intelligence, argues that AI has been stuck in a decades-long rut. His prescription for progress? Teach machines to understand the question why.

title: A Chemist Shines Light on a Surprising Prime Number Pattern
description: When a crystallographer treated prime numbers as a system of particles, the resulting diffraction pattern created a new view of existing conjectures in number theory.

title: Vaccines Are Pushing Pathogens to Evolve
description: Just as antibiotics have bred resistance in bacteria, vaccines can potentially lose their effectiveness over diseases they controlled. Researchers are working to head off the evolution of new threats.

title: Artificial Neural Nets Grow Brainlike Navigation Cells
description: Faced with a navigational challenge, neural networks spontaneously evolved units resembling the grid cells that help living animals find their way.

title: A Thermodynamic Answer to Why Birds Migrate
description: New modeling studies suggest that birds migrate to strike a favorable balance between their input and output of energy.

title: Three Decades Later, Mystery Numbers Explained
description: Zeta values seem to connect distant geometric worlds. In a new proof, mathematicians finally explain why.

title: Cells Talk in a Language That Looks Like Viruses
description: Disease-causing viruses and message-carrying vesicles sit at the ends of a spectrum of membranous particles that cells release.

title: Solution: ‘The DNA Computer Program’
description: Computer code serves as a useful analogy for what our genes do, but the complexity and messiness of life go well beyond simple analogies and mathematical models.

title: Cell by Cell, Scientists Map the Genetic Steps as Eggs Become Animals
description: For the first time, researchers have traced the genetic programs that guide the development of each cell in early embryos. Surprisingly, even cells that start out different can end up the same.

title: First Big Steps Toward Proving the Unique Games Conjecture
description: The latest in a new series of proofs brings theoretical computer scientists within striking distance of one of the great conjectures of their discipline.

title: Chronological Clues to Life’s Early History Lurk in Gene Transfers
description: To date the branches on the evolutionary tree of life, researchers are looking at horizontal gene transfers among ancient microorganisms, which once seemed only to muddle the record.

title: Cells Talk and Help One Another via Tiny Tube Networks
description: Long-overlooked “tunneling nanotubes” and other bridges between cells act as conduits for sharing RNA, proteins or even whole organelles.

title: How Many Genes Do Cells Need? Maybe Almost All of Them
description: An ambitious study in yeast shows that the health of cells depends on the highly intertwined effects of many genes, few of which can be deleted together without consequence.

title: Machine Learning’s ‘Amazing’ Ability to Predict Chaos
description: In new computer experiments, artificial-intelligence algorithms can tell the future of chaotic systems.

title: Decades-Old Graph Problem Yields to Amateur Mathematician
description: By making the first progress on the “chromatic number of the plane” problem in over 60 years, an anti-aging pundit has achieved mathematical immortality.

title: The Elusive Calculus of Insects’ Altruism and Kin Selection
description: How the ultra-cooperative behavior of ants, bees and other social insects could have evolved continues to challenge formal analysis. But a new theory about hedging bets against nature’s unpredictability may change the math and shift the debate.

title: How the DNA Computer Program Makes You and Me
description: Can a set of simple instructions produce complex, three-dimensional living structures?

title: New Brain Maps With Unmatched Detail May Change Neuroscience
description: A technique based on genetic bar codes can easily map the connections of individual brain cells in unprecedented numbers. Unexpected complexity in the visual system is only the first secret it has revealed.

title: Quantum Correlations Reverse Thermodynamic Arrow of Time
description: A recent experiment shows how quantum mechanics can make heat flow from a cold body to a hot one, an apparent (though not real) violation of the second law of thermodynamics.

title: Black Hole Echoes Would Reveal Break With Einstein’s Theory
description: Gravitational waves have opened up new ways to test the properties of black holes — and Einstein’s theory of gravity along with them.

title: Complex Animals Led to More Oxygen, Says Maverick Theory
description: For decades, researchers have commonly assumed that higher oxygen levels led to the sudden diversification of animal life 540 million years ago. But one iconoclast argues the opposite: that new animal behaviors raised oxygen levels and remade the environment.

title: Brainless Embryos Suggest Bioelectricity Guides Growth
description: Researchers are building a case that long before the nervous system works, the brain sends crucial bioelectric signals to guide the growth of embryonic tissues.

title: To Test Einstein’s Equations, Poke a Black Hole
description: Two teams of researchers have made significant progress toward proving the black hole stability conjecture, a critical mathematical test of Einstein’s theory of general relativity.

title: Oxygen and Stem Cells May Have Reshaped Early Complex Animals
description: An unlikely team offers a controversial hypothesis about what enabled animal life to get more complex during the Cambrian explosion.

title: New Giant Viruses Further Blur the Definition of Life
description: A newfound pair of giant viruses have massive genomes and the most complete resources for building proteins ever seen in the viral world. They have refreshed the debate about the origins of these cellular parasites.

title: Solution: ‘When Probability Meets Real Life’
description: When our brains don't have a good intuition for reasoning with numbers, explicit probabilistic thinking can lead to improved decision-making.

title: Why Don’t Patients Get Sick in Sync? Modelers Find Statistical Clues.
description: The long, variable times that some diseases incubate after infection defies simple explanation. An idealized model of tumor growth offers a statistical solution.

title: A Statistical Search for Genomic Truths
description: The computer scientist Barbara Engelhardt develops machine-learning models and methods to scour human genomes for the elusive causes and mechanisms of disease.

title: The Simple Algorithm That Ants Use to Build Bridges
description: Even with no one in charge, army ants work collectively to build bridges out of their bodies. New research reveals the simple rules that lead to such complex group behavior.

title: How Cells Pack Tangled DNA Into Neat Chromosomes
description: For the first time, researchers see how proteins grab loops of DNA and bundle them for cell division. The discovery also hints at how the genome folds to regulate gene expression.

title: Why Artificial Intelligence Like AlphaZero Has Trouble With the Real World
description: The latest artificial intelligence systems start from zero knowledge of a game and grow to world-beating in a matter of hours. But researchers are struggling to apply these systems beyond the arcade.

title: Scant Evidence of Power Laws Found in Real-World Networks
description: A new study challenges one of the most celebrated and controversial ideas in network science.

title: Smart Swarms Seek New Ways to Cooperate
description: New algorithms show how swarms of very simple robots can be made to work together as a group.

title: Neutron Lifetime Puzzle Deepens, but No Dark Matter Seen
description: Two methods of measuring the neutron's longevity give different answers, creating uncertainty in cosmological models. But no one has a clue what the problem is.

title: Evolution Saves Species From ‘Kill the Winner’ Disasters
description: Modelers find evidence that a combination of competition, predation and evolution will push ecosystems toward species diversity anywhere in the universe.

title: When Probability Meets Real Life
description: When faced with a difficult decision, should you go with your gut or carefully calculate the attendant risks?

title: With Strategic Zaps to the Brain, Scientists Boost Memory
description: Stimulating part of the cortex as needed during learning tasks improves later recall. The finding reveals more about the brain's memory network and points toward possible therapies.

title: How Math (and Vaccines) Keep You Safe From the Flu
description: Simple math shows how widespread vaccination can disrupt the exponential spread of disease and prevent epidemics.

title: Job One for Quantum Computers: Boost Artificial Intelligence
description: The fusion of quantum computing and machine learning has become a booming research area. Can it possibly live up to its high expectations?

title: Tissue Engineers Hack Life’s Code for 3-D Folded Shapes
description: Mechanical tension between tethered cells cues developing tissues to fold. Researchers can now program synthetic tissue to make coils, cubes and rippling plates.

title: The Era of Quantum Computing Is Here. Outlook: Cloudy
description: Quantum computers should soon be able to beat classical computers at certain basic tasks. But before they’re truly powerful, researchers have to overcome a number of fundamental roadblocks.

title: A Domesticated Dingo? No, but Some Are Getting Less Wild
description: Near an Australian desert mining camp, wild dingoes are losing their fear of humans. Their genetic and behavioral changes may echo those from the domestication of dogs.

title: Fossil Discoveries Challenge Ideas About Earth’s Start
description: A series of fossil finds suggests that life on Earth started earlier than anyone thought, calling into question a widely held theory of the solar system’s beginnings.

title: Simpler Math Tames the Complexity of Microbe Networks
description: The dizzying network of interactions within microbe communities can defy analysis. But a new approach simplifies the math and makes progress possible.

title: A Neurobiologist Thinks Big — and Small
description: By developing new tools for visualizing subcellular structure and activity in molecular detail, Ed Boyden advances on his goal of understanding how the brain works.

title: What Makes the Hardest Equations in Physics So Difficult?
description: The Navier-Stokes equations describe simple, everyday phenomena, like water flowing from a garden hose, yet they provide a million-dollar mathematical challenge.

title: With ‘Downsized’ DNA, Flowering Plants Took Over the World
description: Compact genomes and tiny cells gave flowering plants an edge over competing flora. This discovery hints at a broader evolutionary principle.

title: Astronomers Trace Radio Burst to Extreme Cosmic Neighborhood
description: A mysterious object that repeatedly bursts with ultra-powerful radio waves must live in an extreme environment — something like the one around a supermassive black hole.

title: Is a Bigger Genetic Code Better? Get Ready to Find Out
description: Evolution settled on a genetic code that uses four letters to name 20 amino acids. Synthetic biologists adding new bases to DNA will be free to improve on nature — if they can.

title: Mathematicians Find Wrinkle in Famed Fluid Equations
description: Two mathematicians prove that under certain extreme conditions, the Navier-Stokes equations output nonsense.

title: New Bird Species Arises From Hybrids, as Scientists Watch
description: The rapid, unorthodox emergence of a new finch in the Galápagos hints that speciation isn’t rare. New hybrid species may quietly appear and disappear without anyone noticing.

title: Solution: ‘Triumph or Cooperation in Game Theory and Evolution’
description: How well does the Nash equilibrium concept from game theory map to the real world?

title: What Bacteria Can Tell Us About Human Evolution
description: To discover our species’ deep history and to shape its future health, we should learn from the microbes that accompanied us on our evolutionary journey.

title: How Bacteria Help Regulate Blood Pressure
description: Kidneys sniff out signals from gut bacteria for cues to lower blood pressure after meals. Our understanding of how the symbiotic microbes affect health is becoming much more molecular.

title: A Physicist’s Physicist Ponders the Nature of Reality
description: Edward Witten reflects on the meaning of dualities in physics and math, emergent space-time, and the pursuit of a complete description of nature.

title: Bacteria Sacrifice DNA Repair for Better RNA
description: Preserving its DNA ought to be a cell’s top priority. But bacteria slow their DNA repair to a crawl in favor of proofreading gene transcripts.

title: New Model Warns About CRISPR Gene Drives in the Wild
description: Two new papers urge caution in using powerful genome-editing technology against invasive species: Models show that aggressive gene drives can’t be contained in the wild.

title: Choosy Eggs May Pick Sperm for Their Genes, Defying Mendel’s Law
description: The oldest law of genetics says that gametes combine randomly, but experiments hint that sometimes eggs select sperm actively for their genetic assets.

title: Seeing the Beautiful Intelligence of Microbes
description: Bacterial biofilms and slime molds are more than crude patches of goo. Detailed time-lapse microscopy reveals how they sense and explore their surroundings, communicate with their neighbors and adaptively reshape themselves.

title: How to Triumph and Cooperate in Game Theory and Evolution
description: In applying game theory to biology and human behavior, have scientists focused too much on competition over cooperation?

title: A Zombie Gene Protects Elephants From Cancer
description: Elephants did not evolve to become huge animals until after they turned a bit of genetic junk into a unique defense against inevitable tumors.

title: From the Edge of the Universe to the Inside of a Proton
description: The Zoomable Universe, a new book by the astrobiologist Caleb Scharf, the illustrator Ron Miller and 5W Infographics, tours the universe’s 62 orders of magnitude.

title: Solution: ‘How to Win at Deep Learning’
description: When equipped with hidden layers, deep neural networks can accomplish nonlinear feats that are difficult even with sophisticated mathematics.

title: Life’s First Molecule Was Protein, Not RNA, New Model Suggests
description: Which mattered first at the dawn of life: proteins or nucleic acids? Proteins may have had the edge if a theorized process let them grow long enough to become self-replicating catalysts.

title: How to Build a Robot That Wants to Change the World
description: And not destroy humanity in the process.

title: The Atomic Theory of Origami
description: By reimagining the kinks and folds of origami as atoms in a lattice, researchers are uncovering strange behavior hiding in simple structures.

title: The Unforgiving Math That Stops Epidemics
description: If you didn't get a flu shot, you are endangering more than just your own health. Calculations of herd immunity against common diseases don't make exceptions.

title: Insects Conquered a Watery Realm With Just Two New Genes
description: Minor genetic changes can have big evolutionary consequences. When a gene duplication gave some water striders a novel leg part, it opened up a new world for them.

title: Artificial Intelligence Learns to Learn Entirely on Its Own
description: A new version of AlphaGo needed no human instruction to figure out how to clobber the best Go player in the world — itself.

title: Simple Bacteria Offer Clues to the Origins of Photosynthesis
description: Studies of the energy-harvesting proteins in primitive cells suggest that key features of photosynthesis might have evolved a billion years earlier than scientists thought.

title: Neutron-Star Collision Shakes Space-Time and Lights Up the Sky
description: Astronomers have for the first time matched a gravitational-wave signal to a kilonova’s burst of light, observations that will “go down in the history of astronomy.”

title: How to Win at Deep Learning
description: What happens when you increase the number of layers in an artificial neural network?

description: The American physicists Rainer Weiss, Kip Thorne and Barry Barish were honored for dreaming up and realizing the experiment that confirmed the existence of gravitational waves.

title: Genetic Struggles Within Cells May Create New Species
description: Mitonuclear conflict — a struggle between the genes in a cell’s nucleus and its mitochondria — might sometimes split species in two.

title: Moonshine Link Discovered for Pariah Symmetries
description: A type of symmetry so unusual that it was called a “pariah” turns out to have deep connections to number theory.

title: Genetics Spills Secrets From Neanderthals’ Lost History
description: How many Neanderthals were there? Archaeology and genetics have given very different answers. A new study reconciles them and reveals the lost history of these ancient people — including an early brush with extinction.

title: Viruses Would Rather Jump to New Hosts Than Evolve With Them
description: The discovery that viruses move between species unexpectedly often is rewriting ideas about their evolutionary history — and may have troubling implications for the threat from emerging diseases.

title: Mathematicians Measure Infinities and Find They’re Equal
description: Two mathematicians have proved that two different infinities are equal in size, settling a long-standing question. Their proof rests on a surprising link between the sizes of infinities and the complexity of mathematical theories.

title: To Solve the Biggest Mystery in Physics, Join Two Kinds of Law
description: Reductionism breaks the world into elementary building blocks. Emergence finds the simple laws that arise out of complexity. These two complementary ways of viewing the universe come together in modern theories of quantum gravity.

title: Bacteria Use Brainlike Bursts of Electricity to Communicate
description: With electrical signals, simple cells organize themselves into complex societies and negotiate with other colonies.

title: Seeing Emergent Physics Behind Evolution
description: Nigel Goldenfeld applies the physics of condensed matter to understand how evolution sprinted for the earliest life — and then slowed down.

title: The Oldest Mini-Brains Have Lifelike Young Cells
description: "Organoid" brain tissue models grown in a lab for two years can help scientists study a critical period of development just before and after birth.

title: Jason Morgan Recalls Discovering Earth’s Tectonic Plates
description: Jason Morgan developed the theory of plate tectonics in 1967 while working among a critical mass of talented geophysicists at Princeton University.

title: Interspecies Hybrids Play a Vital Role in Evolution
description: Hybrids, once treated as biological misfits, play a vital role in the evolution of many animal species. Now conservationists are trying to reconcile that truth with policies.

title: A Physicist Who Models ISIS and the Alt-Right
description: The rise of new extremist groups has served as both an impetus and test-case for Neil Johnson’s models of terrorism and insurgency.

title: Mathematicians Tame Rogue Waves, Lighting Up Future of LEDs
description: The mathematician Svitlana Mayboroda and collaborators have figured out how to predict the behavior of electrons — a mathematical discovery that could have immediate practical effects.

title: Beating the Odds for Lucky Mutations
description: If DNA repair makes useful mutations more likely, it could accelerate cells’ adaptations to harsh environments.

title: New Shapes Solve Infinite Pool-Table Problem
description: Two “rare jewels” have illuminated a mysterious multidimensional object that connects a huge variety of mathematical work.

description: Take chemistry, add energy, get life. The first tests of Jeremy England’s provocative origin-of-life hypothesis are in, and they appear to show how order can arise from nothing.

title: Building Codes for Bacterial Cities
description: Hydrodynamics and competition guide the architectural design of biofilm fortresses.

title: Cell Atlases Reveal Biology’s Frontiers
description: New techniques expose unexpected diversity within seemingly uniform tissues.

title: Why Are There Two Sexes?
description: Asexual reproduction can produce twice as many offspring as sexual reproduction without the hassle of finding and courting a mate. So why do most complex animals have two sexes? Why not three?

title: How Nature Solves Problems Through Computation
description: The evolutionary biologist Jessica Flack seeks the computational rules that groups of organisms use to solve problems.

title: Strange Noise in Gravitational-Wave Data Sparks Debate
description: The team that discovered gravitational waves put their data online. Now an independent group of researchers claims that they’ve found what might be a serious problem.

title: Can Microbes Encourage Altruism?
description: If gut bacteria can sway their hosts to be selfless, it could answer a riddle that goes back to Darwin.

title: Solution: ‘Bongard Problems and Scientific Discovery’
description: Like scientific puzzles, Bongard problems can lead you through a frustrating blind search until you find that simple, elegant rule that fits a seemingly random pattern.

title: Moonlighting Genes Evolve for a Venomous Job
description: An unexpected mechanism allows wasps to rapidly co-opt genes for new toxic functions.

title: Researchers Check Space-Time to See if It’s Made of Quantum Bits
description: The newly developed theory of emergent gravity, proposed as an alternative to dark matter, struggles in one of its first trials.

title: Rainer Weiss, Remembering the Little Room in the Plywood Palace
description: The physicist who designed the LIGO experiment that detected gravitational waves still holes up in a small basement lab surrounded by electronics and optical instruments.

title: The Thorny Truth About Spine Evolution
description: A definitive explanation for why plants evolved spines remains elusive, and human biases compound the problem.

title: How Superfluid Dark Matter Mimics an Old Idea About Gravity
description: Does the force of gravity change at large scales? Perhaps not, but a new theory of dark matter shows why that could appear to be the case.

title: Dark Matter Recipe Calls for One Part Superfluid
description: A different kind of dark matter could help to resolve an old celestial conundrum.

title: Bongard Problems and Scientific Discovery
description: For your frustration, joy and entertainment, our puzzle challenges you to find general patterns or rules based on seemingly random, specific examples.

title: Sylvia Earle Is Not Done Exploring
description: The legendary marine biologist discusses why she’s excited about the coming era of ocean science, the shortsightedness of maritime exploitation and diving in the Arctic in her 80s.

title: Wanted: More Data, the Dirtier the Better
description: The computational immunologist Purvesh Khatri embraces messy data as a way to capture the messiness of disease. As a result, he’s making elusive genomic discoveries.

title: Solution: ‘Darwinian Evolution Explains Lamarckism’
description: How Darwinian natural selection can produce and sustain a Lamarckian “inheritance of acquired characteristics.”

title: Latest Black Hole Collision Comes With a Twist
description: The Advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory’s third detection further compounds the mystery of why black holes collide.

title: A Puzzle of Clever Connections Nears a Happy End
description: The three young friends who devised the “happy ending” problem would become some of the most influential mathematicians of the 20th century, but were never able to solve their own puzzle. Now it receives its first big breakthrough.

title: Awash in Sea of Data, Ecologists Turn to Open Access Tools
description: To assess the ocean’s health, ecology’s “rugged individualists” learned to get with the big data program.

title: Why Quantum Computers Might Not Break Cryptography
description: A new paper claims that a common digital security system could be tweaked to withstand attacks even from a powerful quantum computer.

title: Can Darwinian Evolution Explain Lamarckism?
description: Answering three questions can help reveal how the “inheritance of acquired characteristics” fits into modern evolutionary theory.

title: How Heat Kills Cells
description: The proteins that unravel as the temperature starts to rise turn out to be among the most vital.

title: Swirling Bacteria Linked to the Physics of Phase Transitions
description: The new experiments suggest that simple models can explain the behavior of thousands of interacting organisms.

title: The Quantum Thermodynamics Revolution
description: As physicists extend the 19th-century laws of thermodynamics to the quantum realm, they’re rewriting the relationships among energy, entropy and information.

title: Solution: ‘Friday the 13th’
description: There’s more than one good way to bring order to our unruly, seemingly arbitrary calendar.

title: The Secret Power of the Cell’s Waste Bin
description: Trash collectors in the cell moonlight at the controls of the genetic machinery.

title: A Cosmic Burst Repeats, Deepen­ing a Mystery
description: After a surprise discovery, astrophysicists are racing to understand superenergetic flashes of radio waves that sometimes beep out from distant galaxies.

title: A Simple Visual Proof of a Powerful Idea
description: Ramsey’s theorem predicts a surprising (and useful) consistency in the organization of graphs. Here’s a simple visual proof of how it works.

title: Is It Friday the 13th Again?
description: How our society defines years, months and weeks can seem frustratingly arbitrary. Can you bring order to our unruly calendar?

title: Solution: ‘A Ticking Evolutionary Clock’
description: How to calculate when a gene’s rate of evolution will slow to a crawl.

title: Quantum Questions Inspire New Math
description: In order to fully understand the quantum world, we may have to develop a new realm of mathematics.

title: Yves Meyer, Wavelet Expert, Wins Abel Prize
description: The French mathematician was cited “for his pivotal role in the development of the mathematical theory of wavelets.”

title: A Ticking Evolutionary Clock
description: How quickly will a gene’s rate of evolution slow to a crawl?

title: Evolution Runs Faster on Short Timescales
description: Examine evolution over the course of years or centuries, and you’ll find that it progresses much more quickly than it does over geologic time.

title: ‘Digital Alchemist’ Seeks Rules of Emergence
description: Computational physicist Sharon Glotzer is uncovering the rules by which complex collective phenomena emerge from simple building blocks.

title: Why Did Life Move to Land? For the View
description: The ancient creatures who first crawled onto land may have been lured by the informational benefit that comes from seeing through air.

title: In Mathematics, ‘You Cannot Be Lied To’
description: For Sylvia Serfaty, mathematics is all about truth and beauty and building scientific and human connections.

title: How Circadian Clocks Differ From Sleep
description: The circadian clock is in nearly every cell, and researchers have untangled many of its secrets. But sleep has been harder to pin down.

title: How Life (and Death) Spring From Disorder
description: Life was long thought to obey its own set of rules. But as simple systems show signs of lifelike behavior, scientists are arguing about whether this apparent complexity is all a consequence of thermodynamics.

title: How Viruses May Have Led to Complex Life
description: Without viruses, we might never have evolved.

title: Droplets That ‘Come to Life’
description: Life might have originated in droplets that behave surprisingly like living cells.

title: Dividing Droplets Could Explain Life’s Origin
description: Researchers have discovered that simple “chemically active” droplets grow to the size of cells and spontaneously divide, suggesting they might have evolved into the first living cells.

title: The Shape-Shifting Army Inside Your Cells
description: Proteins work like rigid keys to activate cellular functions — or so everyone thought. Scientists are discovering a huge number of proteins that shape-shift to do their work, upending a century-old maxim of biology.

title: Graph Isomorphism Vanquished — Again
description: Just five days after posting a retraction, László Babai announced that he had fixed the error in his landmark graph isomorphism algorithm.

title: Complexity Theory Problem Strikes Back
description: The legendary graph isomorphism problem may be harder than a 2015 result seemed to suggest.

title: Finding the Actions That Alter Evolution
description: The biologist Marcus Feldman creates mathematical models that reveal how cultural traditions can affect the evolution of a species.

title: 3-D Fractals Offer Clues to Complex Systems
description: By folding fractals into 3-D objects, a mathematical duo hopes to gain new insight into simple equations.

title: Explorers Find Passage to Earth’s Dark Age
description: Geochemical signals from deep inside Earth are beginning to shed light on the planet’s first 50 million years, a formative period long viewed as inaccessible to science.

title: Viruses Find a New Way to Hijack Cells
description: A virus that causes crippling birth defects has been shown to do something else: It changes thousands of messages coming from DNA that control normal cellular activities.

title: Scientists Seek to Update Evolution
description: Recent discoveries have led some researchers to argue that the modern evolutionary synthesis needs to be amended.

title: Strange Numbers Found in Particle Collisions
description: An unexpected connection has emerged between the results of physics experiments and an important, seemingly unrelated set of numbers in pure mathematics.

title: Why (Almost) Everyone Was Wrong
description: The results of this year’s presidential election made a mockery of analytical election forecast modelers.

title: What Sonic Black Holes Say About Real Ones
description: Can a fluid analogue of a black hole point physicists toward the theory of quantum gravity, or is it a red herring?

title: A Conductor of Evolution’s Subtle Symphony
description: At first, the biologist Richard Lenski thought his long-term experiment on evolution might last for 2,000 generations. Nearly three decades and over 65,000 generations later, he’s still amazed by evolution’s “awesome inventiveness.”

title: The Cell’s Backup Genetic Instructions
description: The cell is equipped with multiple redundancies in case something goes wrong. Researchers have begun to map these systems.

title: Genetic Architects Untwist DNA’s Turns
description: Researchers have used the gene-editing tool CRISPR to manipulate the way that DNA coils up inside the cell — another step in the quest to understand how the genome’s 3-D structure impacts its function.

title: Solution: ‘Which Forecasts Are True?’
description: Aside from potential clues gleaned from a fluke result, it would take hundreds of U.S. presidential elections to definitely conclude that one election forecasting model is superior to another.

title: Giant Genetic Map Shows Life’s Hidden Links
description: In a monumental set of experiments, spread out over nearly two decades, biologists removed genes two at a time to uncover the secret workings of the cell.

title: A Wormhole Between Physics and Education
description: The theoretical particle physicist Helen Quinn has blazed a singular path from the early days of the Standard Model to the latest overhaul of science education in the United States.

title: Off-the-Shelf Lens Assists Dark Matter Find
description: A camera lens often used by wildlife and sports photographers has helped astronomers learn about dark matter and galaxy formation.

title: Watching Evolution Happen in Two Lifetimes
description: The biologists Rosemary and Peter Grant have spent four decades on a tiny island in the Galápagos. Their discoveries reveal how new animal species can emerge in just a few generations.

title: From Gaia, a Twinkling Treasure Trove
description: The first star map from the ESA’s Gaia space telescope is poised to revolutionize our understanding of the Milky Way galaxy.

title: Responding Rapidly to Big Discoveries
description: How do scientists react to major breaking science news? For astrophysicists after the big gravitational waves announcement, it was meeting for two weeks in Santa Barbara, California.

title: Genetic Engineering to Clash With Evolution
description: Gene drives promise to spread a trait across an entire population. But evolutionary forces are going to alter even the best-engineered plans.

title: Solution: ‘A Drunkard’s Walk in Manhattan’
description: City blocks help illustrate why walking randomly tends to take you away from your starting point.

title: Colliding Black Holes Tell New Story of Stars
description: Just months after their discovery, gravitational waves coming from the mergers of black holes are shaking up astrophysics.

title: The Strange Case of Typhoid Mary
description: The infamous case of Typhoid Mary underscores the importance of tolerance in understanding disease.

title: A New Way to Predict Infection’s Toll
description: Scientists have developed new ways to forecast who will bounce back from disease by studying not just the way the immune system fights infections, but how the body repairs itself.

title: A Drunkard’s Walk in Manhattan
description: Why is it that when you walk randomly, the more you walk, the farther you get from your starting point?

title: Jammed Cells Expose the Physics of Cancer
description: The subtle mechanics of densely packed cells may help explain why some cancerous tumors stay put while others break off and spread through the body.

title: Air Traffic Control for Random Surfaces
description: Mathematicians have had a hard time finding commonalities in large groups of random shapes — until recently.

title: Moonshine Master Toys With String Theory
description: The physicist-mathematician Miranda Cheng is working to harness a mysterious connection between string theory, algebra and number theory.

title: A Unified Theory of Randomness
description: Researchers have uncovered deep connections among different types of random objects, illuminating hidden geometric structures.

title: How to Grow a New Model Organism
description: To develop new model organisms, scientists will have to find species that are easy to grow in the lab.

title: Biologists Search for New Model Organisms
description: The bulk of biological research is centered on a handful of species. Are we missing a huge chunk of interesting biology?

title: Mining Black Hole Collisions for New Physics
description: The physicist Asimina Arvanitaki is thinking up ways to search gravitational wave data for evidence of dark matter particles orbiting black holes.

title: Faster Evolution on a Warmer Earth
description: When life first emerged roughly 4 billion years ago, DNA may have been a much more malleable molecule.

title: A Bird’s-Eye View of Nature’s Hidden Order
description: Scientists are exploring a mysterious pattern, found in birds’ eyes, boxes of marbles and other surprising places, that is neither regular nor random.

title: New Lizard Shows Evolution’s Predictability
description: A newly discovered anole on the island of Hispaniola confirms that the buildup of ecological communities can follow predictable patterns.

title: The Oracle of Arithmetic
description: At 28, Peter Scholze is uncovering deep connections between number theory and geometry.

title: New Life Found That Lives Off Electricity
description: Scientists have figured out how microbes can suck energy from rocks. Such lifeforms might be more widespread than anyone anticipated.

title: LIGO Reports Second Black-Hole Merger
description: The spokesperson for the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory called it “a promising start to mapping the populations of black holes in our universe.”

title: An Explorer of Quantum Borderlands
description: Suchitra Sebastian’s searches for quantum anomalies have led to the potential discovery of a new building block of matter.

title: Evidence of a ‘Fifth Force’ Faces Scrutiny
description: A lab in Hungary has reported an anomaly that could lead to a physics revolution. But even as excitement builds, closer scrutiny has unearthed a troubling backstory.

title: Solution: ‘A Random Place at the Table’
description: Try these shortcuts for solving problems that seem to require a lengthy calculation.

title: How Neanderthal DNA Helps Humanity
description: Neanderthals and Denisovans may have endowed modern humans with genetic variants that helped them thrive in new environments.

title: Mathematicians Bridge Finite-Infinite Divide
description: A surprising new proof is helping to connect the mathematics of infinity to the physical world.

title: New Support for Alternative Quantum View
